questions.question: What are the characteristics or functions of ServiceNow IntegrationHub ETL? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Integrates third-party data into the CMDB or into non-CM DB tables

options.label: B
options.text: Uses the IRE to process and integrate data

options.label: C
options.text: Imports Microsoft SCCM/Intune data into the CMDB

options.label: D
options.text: Performs discovery data collection and updates the CMDB

questions.explanation: IntegrationHub ETL is built to bring external/third-party data into ServiceNow, landing it either in the CMDB or in supported non-CMDB tables, and it routes that data through the Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE) so CIs are matched and reconciled rather than blindly inserted. Importing SCCM/Intune data is handled by a dedicated Service Graph Connector, not ETL generically, and Discovery (not ETL) performs active data collection.

questions.question:
User endpoint devices are imported into the CMDB and populate the **Assigned to** [assigned_to] field on the Computer [cmdb_ci_computer] CI. The Asset team requests that Configuration Analysts populate the **Assigned to** field on the related Asset.

What action should a Configuration Analyst take to accomplish this automatically?

options.label: A
options.text: Use the Asset-CI Field Mapping module to create a new rule to replicate the ‘Assigned to’ value between the asset and associated CI

options.label: B
options.text: Hide the ‘Assigned to’ field on the asset record and create a new field that dot walks to the related CI to get the ‘Assigned to’ value

options.label: C
options.text: Configure a business rule on the computer table to use a script to populate the ‘Assigned to’ filed on the asset based on insert or update in the computer class ‘Assigned to’ field

questions.explanation:
Asset-CI Field Mapping is the supported mechanism for synchronizing fields between an Asset and its logically associated Configuration Item. A mapping for **Assigned to** replicates updates between the related asset and Computer CI automatically, without a custom business rule or a replacement display-only field.

**Learn more:** [Map asset and CI fields](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-asset-management/asset-management/t_CreateAssetandCIFieldsMapping.html) · [Asset and CI management](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/it-service-management/asset-management/c_ManagingAssets.html)

questions.question:
A Configuration Manager has configured multiple data sources, all authorized to update the same class and the same set of class attributes in the CMDB.

What can the Configuration Manager do to control which data source should be the authoritative source of truth for a specific class or set of class attributes?

options.label: A
options.text: Assign a priority to each data source in the reconciliation rules

options.label: B
options.text: Manually run the data source updates in the correct order

options.label: C
options.text: Configure data refresh rules with a specific time period

options.label: D
options.text: Assign a run order to each data source in the identification rules

questions.explanation:
Static CMDB reconciliation rules specify both which data sources are authorized to update class attributes and their precedence. Assigning priorities to the authorized sources determines the authoritative source: a higher-priority source can update an attribute over a lower-priority source.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow — Reconciliation rules](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/r_ReconciliationRulesPrinciples.html)

questions.question: Match each CMDB Health Dashboard metric to its description.

options.label: A
options.text: Use these to compare actual values with expected values -> Audits

options.label: B
options.text: Use of these should be minimized -> Required fields

options.label: C
options.text: Certain attribute values are not set, or relationships are missing -> Orphan CIs

options.label: D
options.text: Preferable for them to be populated, as they could be useful in troubleshooting issues -> Recommended fields

options.label: E
options.text: Have not been updated and may be outdated -> Stale CIs

options.label: F
options.text: Detected during identification and reconciliation and have associated base system remediation tools -> Duplicate CIs

questions.explanation:
Audits evaluate actual field values against expected values. Required fields are mandatory, so their use should be limited; recommended fields are optional but useful for troubleshooting. Orphan rules identify CIs missing key attributes or relationships. Stale CIs have not been updated within the configured duration. Duplicate CIs are evaluated using identification rules and can be remediated with de-duplication tools.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow CMDB Health KPIs and metrics](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/r_CMDBHealthMetrics.html) · [ServiceNow CMDB glossary](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb-glossary.html)

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator wants only CIs from Principal Classes to appear in CI reference fields, such as the CI reference fields available from an Incident Form.

Where does the CMDB Administrator designate Principal Classes?
questions.explanation:
Principal-class status is configured on an individual CI class in **CI Class Manager**, under the class’s Basic Info settings. Marking a class as principal enables the Principal Class filter, which restricts Configuration Item lists and reference fields to CIs from those designated classes.

**Learn more:** [Update class list in the Principal Class filter](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/en-US/bundle/zurich-servicenow-platform/page/product/configuration-management/task/update-principal-class-filter.html)

questions.question:
A customer wants to model their business applications and would like to capture different types of data that includes Personally Identifiable Information (PII) data.

Based on these requirements, which CMDB class needs to be leveraged to achieve this?
questions.explanation: CSDM models sensitive or regulated data types, such as PII, as Information Objects, which are logical representations of data assets that can be related to the Business Applications that process or store them. API Component, Business Capability, and Data Classification are used for other purposes in CSDM and do not represent a data asset itself.

questions.question:
The Application Portfolio Management team is asking for help modeling platforms as Business Applications.

How would this be mapped in CSDM using the ServiceNow Platform in the Incident and Change applications?

options.label: A
options.text: ServiceNow Platform, Incident, and Change would all be web based Architecture type.Incident and Change would have a reference to ServiceNow Platform.

options.label: B
options.text: ServiceNow Platform would be an Architecture type of Platform Host.Incident and Change would be Platform Applications and have a reference to ServiceNow Platform.

options.label: C
options.text: ServiceNow Platform, Incident, and Change would all be web based Architecture type.A Depends On relationship would be created between ServiceNow Platform and Incident and Change.

options.label: D
options.text: ServiceNow Platform would be an Architecture type of Platform Host.Incident and Change would be Platform Applications.Then a Depends On relationship would be created between ServiceNow Platform and Incident and Change.

questions.explanation: In CSDM, platforms are modeled using a dedicated Platform-to-Application hierarchy: the ServiceNow Platform is designated as a Platform Host (architecture type), while Incident and Change are typed as Platform Applications. This structure uses a native reference field directly linking Platform Applications to their Platform Host, which is structurally distinct from Depends On relationships used elsewhere in the model.

questions.question:
A Service Desk Manager wants to leverage the Unified Map to find active incidents or problems for a selected CI.

Which panel will give the manager visibility and details?
questions.explanation: The Related items module in the Unified Map's contextual side panel groups records tied to the selected (or home) CI into categories such as active incidents, problems, and changes, giving exactly the visibility the manager needs. The Overview and Attributes panels show CI properties rather than related-record activity. **Learn more:** [View related items for a CI](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/bundle/xanadu-servicenow-platform/page/product/configuration-management/task/unified-map-show-related-items.html)

questions.question:
The CMDB Administrator has been asked to establish Configuration Management with a functional CMDB.

Which factor is most critical for successfully operationalizing the CMDB in ServiceNow?

options.label: A
options.text: Populating the CMDB with as much data as possible to ensure a comprehensive inventory of CIs

options.label: B
options.text: Establishing clear governance and continuously monitoring CMDB health

options.label: C
options.text: Allowing IT teams to modify CMDB records as needed to promote flexibility in data management

options.label: D
options.text: Relying on automated discovery tools to maintain and update CMDB records

questions.explanation: Operationalizing a functional CMDB depends on establishing clear governance (ownership, policies, and standard operating procedures) combined with continuous monitoring of CMDB health, rather than a one-time cleanup or data-loading exercise. Simply maximizing data volume, allowing unrestricted edits, or relying solely on discovery without governance does not sustain a trustworthy, usable CMDB over time.

questions.question:
A CSDM Data Manager needs metrics on the alignment of Technology Management Services (Technical Services) and Technology Management Offerings (Technical Service Offerings) with best practices.

Which tab in the CSDM Data Foundation Dashboard provides this information?
questions.explanation: In the CSDM maturity framework (Crawl, Walk, Run, Fly), Technology Management Services and Technology Management Offerings are positioned within the Walk stage. Walk represents the intermediate maturity level where service-to-supporting-technology alignments and service offering structures are defined and managed.

questions.question:
The Incident Process Owner asks which classes of CSDM are used on the Incident form.

Which classes are appropriate? (select 2)
questions.explanation: On the Incident form the impacted-service reference is populated with either the Application Service (the technical service affected) or the Service Offering (how that service is consumed by a given group), which is why CSDM guidance keeps Business Application and Service Portfolio, both governance/portfolio constructs, off operational incident records.

questions.question: Which shows the most complete list of policy types that are provided by the CMDB Data Manager?

options.label: D
options.text: Retire, Archive, Attestation, Certification, and Delete

questions.explanation: CMDB Data Manager provides five policy types - Retire, Archive, Attestation, Certification, and Delete - each driven by scheduled jobs and lifecycle rules that act on the CI classes they target.

questions.question: Which are CMDB Data Manager end of life policy types? (select 2)
questions.explanation: CMDB Data Manager supports Archive and Retire as end-of-life policy types. Archive policies move records to archive tables for compliance and performance optimization, while Retire policies mark CIs as retired for historical tracking. Lost, Decommission, and Disposed are not standard Data Manager policy types.

questions.question:
A Configuration Manager wants to use the Unified Map.

Where can it be accessed?
questions.explanation:
Unified Map is available in CMDB Workspace, where users can open it from the Quick Links section to visualize CMDB configuration items and their relationships.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Unified Map](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/unified-map/cmdb-workspace-unified-map.html)

questions.question:
A Configuration Manager working in the CMDB Workspace wants to see how CIs are connected to each other.

Which tool can be used?
questions.explanation: The Unified Map in CMDB Workspace combines the legacy Dependency Views and Service Mapping topology views into one interface, letting a Configuration Manager explore how any CI relates to upstream and downstream CIs. It is the designated tool for visualizing CI-to-CI relationships within CMDB Workspace, unlike a Business Service Map, which is scoped to a single business service's structure. **Learn more:** [CMDB Workspace Unified Map](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb-workspace-unified-map.html)

questions.question: How does a CMDB Administrator use the ServiceNow Platform to ensure the data quality associated with CIs in the CMDB?
questions.explanation: The CMDB Workspace is the primary tool for ensuring CI data quality. It provides access to the CMDB Health Dashboard with Correctness and Completeness scorecards, enabling administrators to identify, analyze, and remediate data quality issues across the configuration database.

questions.question:
An organization is using CMDB Query Builder to find all application services with a database that has incidents and all infrastructure in those application services.

Which steps does the organization take to build this query? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Use a CMDB Query to include application services and their related infrastructure

options.label: B
options.text: Use a Service Mapping Query to find all incidents related to the database

options.label: C
options.text: Use a Service Mapping Query to include non-CMDB tables like the Incident table

options.label: D
options.text: Add a non-CMDB table to the query

questions.explanation: CMDB Query Builder starts from a CMDB Query that traverses relationships from application services down to their related infrastructure, giving the CI-based portion of the result. Because the Incident table is not a CMDB table, it must be explicitly added from the Non-CMDB Tables list and joined to the query pattern to bring in incident data tied to the database CIs; there is no separate "Service Mapping Query" object in Query Builder, which is why the options referencing it are incorrect.

questions.question:
The CMDB Administrator group wants the CMDB Health Dashboard Compliance Scorecard to show meaningful results for server records that are not on the latest patch.

What must be configured to accomplish this?

options.label: A
options.text: Certification Policies, Data Filters, Scheduled Jobs

options.label: D
options.text: Technical Service Offerings, Dynamic CI Groups, CMDB Groups

questions.explanation: The CMDB Health Dashboard Compliance Scorecard requires configuration of certification mechanisms: defining certification filters to identify the target population (unpatched servers), creating certification templates to specify compliance rules, and setting up audits to run compliance checks and populate scorecard results.

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator viewing the CMDB Data Foundations Dashboard finds that the Unique Locations Result percentage is low.

What process does the associated playbook recommend to resolve this issue?

options.label: A
options.text: Review both locations, update CIs with the correct location and delete the duplicate location

options.label: B
options.text: Retain the location that matches the organization’s standard naming convention, and delete the duplicate without further validation

options.label: C
options.text: Keep both locations as either can be used as a valid alternate location

options.label: D
options.text: Use the Duplicate CI Remediator the merge the duplicate location records

questions.explanation:
The Unique Locations metric identifies duplicate nonempty names in Location [cmn_location] records. Remediation requires validating which location is correct, repointing affected CIs to that location, and deleting the duplicate record so that CI location references remain accurate.

**Learn more:** [CMDB Data Foundations dashboard](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb-data-foundations-dashboard.html?contentId=W3jznFFdpcXU5nbjXnCNqQ)

questions.question:
A new ServiceNow customer is forming a Configuration Management team to support its CMDB.

Match each role with its corresponding job description.

options.label: A
options.text: Has read-only access to CMDB data and to basic user interface such as CMDB reports and dashboards -> CMDB Process Owner

options.label: B
options.text: Accountable for managing all elements that make up a portfolio throughout their entire lifecycle -> Service or Product Owner

options.label: C
options.text: Manages assigned CI tables and keeps records updated and resolves tasks related to CMDB records -> CI Analyst

options.label: D
options.text: Obtains highest level role for CMDB privileges -> Configuration Manager/CMDB Admin

questions.explanation:
The CMDB Process Owner uses CMDB data and basic reporting interfaces without performing administrative maintenance. The Service or Product Owner owns the portfolio lifecycle. CI Analysts perform the operational work of maintaining assigned CI records and resolving related tasks. Configuration Managers/CMDB Admins use the CMDB administrator role, which provides the highest level of CMDB access and privileges.

questions.question:
An IT group has a requirement to upgrade all the Windows servers. There is a Dynamic CI Group containing all the Windows servers.

What happens to the Dynamic CI Group when it is referenced from the Configuration Item field on a Change form?

options.label: A
options.text: It displays all related CIs in the Impacted Services related list.

options.label: B
options.text: It calculates impact against the Dynamic CI Group.

options.label: C
options.text: It displays all related CIs in the Affected CIs related list.

questions.explanation: Selecting a Dynamic CI Group in the Configuration Item field of a Change form automatically expands its membership into the Change's Affected CIs related list, so all of the Windows servers the group currently contains are listed as affected by the change.

questions.question:
A service owner uses Unified Map to understand the composition of a service, but wants to filter out irrelevant information.

Which options are available to the service owner in the filter panel? (select 2)
questions.explanation:
Unified Map supports filters for discovery source and CI class (CI type), allowing service-map content to be narrowed to relevant configuration items.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Unified Map documentation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/unified-map/cmdb-workspace-unified-map.html)

questions.question:
The Configuration Management team wants to confirm that all servers in the CMDB actually exist in the data center.

Which CMDB Data Manager policy type would the team create?
questions.explanation: An Attestation policy in CMDB Data Manager generates tasks asking a responsible person or group to explicitly confirm that a CI still exists, is still relevant, and is properly owned, which is exactly the verification the team needs for its servers. Retire, Delete, and Archive are lifecycle actions for CIs already known to be obsolete, while Certification is aimed at broader regulatory/accuracy checks rather than simple existence confirmation.

questions.question:
A CMDB Manager uses CMDB 360/Multisource CMDB to maintain and improve CMDB quality.

Why would the Manager use CMDB 360/Multisource CMDB?

options.label: A
options.text: To identify CI attributes from multiple data sources

options.label: B
options.text: To ingest data from multiple data sources using Import Set(s)

options.label: C
options.text: To populate the CMDB from multiple data sources

options.label: D
options.text: To ingest data from multiple data sources using Service Graph Connector(s)

questions.explanation: CMDB 360 (Multisource CMDB) is a comparison and investigation tool that shows how different discovery and integration sources report values for the same CI, helping a manager identify gaps, conflicts, and differing attribute values across those sources. Ingesting or populating CMDB data is instead the job of Import Sets, Service Graph Connectors, or Discovery, not CMDB 360 itself.

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator wants to minimize stale CIs in the CMDB.

Which CMDB Health Dashboard scorecard shows this information?
questions.explanation:
The Correctness scorecard includes the staleness metric, which measures the percentage of stale CIs and aggregates that result into the Correctness KPI.

**Learn more:** [Create a CMDB Health staleness rule](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/t_CreateCMDBHealthStaleRule.html) · [CMDB Health KPIs and metrics](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/r_CMDBHealthMetrics.html)

questions.question:
A Configuration Management team needs to prevent duplicate server records to avoid confusion among users. Server records are identified when they are processed via the Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE) using the configured identification rules.

Where would these rules be configured?
questions.explanation: Identification rules used by the Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE) are defined per CI class, and CI Class Manager is the interface used to view and configure each class's Identification Rule (criterion attributes and identifier entries). The Health Dashboard and Data Manager are for monitoring and bulk data operations, not for defining identification logic, and the CMDB Workspace is a browsing/visualization tool.

questions.question:
An organization is relocating its data centers and needs to understand the effects of the proposed changes.

How can Application Service Mapping be used as part of Change Management?

options.label: A
options.text: To understand the physical location of CIs

options.label: B
options.text: To identify which devices will go offline first

options.label: C
options.text: To understand the business impact of CIs

questions.explanation: Application Service Mapping exposes dependency relationships between configuration items and the application and business services they support, enabling change impact analysis to determine the business impact of affected CIs.

questions.question:
A Configuration Manager must use a policy type to automatically create and assign tasks that verify the existence of CIs.

Which policy type should be used to meet this goal?
questions.explanation:
An Attestation policy assigns tasks for users to verify the physical existence of the IT infrastructure or applications represented by CIs. Certification is used to verify specified data attributes, whereas Retire and Delete govern CI lifecycle actions.

**Learn more:** [Working with CMDB Data Manager](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/en-US/bundle/zurich-servicenow-platform/page/product/configuration-management/concept/cmdb-data-management.html) · [CMDB Data Manager experience in CMDB Workspace and in Service Graph Workspace](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/data-mgr-exp-cmdb-workspace.html)

questions.question:
The Server [cmdb_ci_server] class uses a dynamic reconciliation rule of lowest value for the Disk Space (GB) field, while the Windows Server [cmdb_ci_win_server] class uses a dynamic reconciliation rule of most reported for the Disk Space (GB) field.

Given the following data sources that populate Windows Server data into the CMDB 360/Multisource CMDB:

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783716363959-7ay4rnbq.png)

Which value would be added to the CMDB for the Disk Space (GB) field of a Windows Server [cmdb_ci_win_server] record?
questions.explanation: The Windows Server class reconciles the Disk Space (GB) field using a 'most reported' rule, which keeps the value reported by the largest number of distinct data sources rather than the numerically highest or lowest value. Here 75 GB is reported by two sources (Tivoli and ServiceNow) while 50 GB and 80 GB are each reported by only one source, so 75 GB is the value written to the CMDB.

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator is beginning the journey of populating the CMDB and needs to verify that any data which is no longer useful/applicable is removed.

Which governance management tool will accomplish this?

options.label: B
options.text: CMDB and CSDM Data Foundations Dashboard

questions.explanation: CMDB Data Manager is the policy-driven governance tool used to define lifecycle rules that identify configuration data that is no longer useful or applicable and drive it through retire, archive, or delete actions, replacing the legacy Data Certification approach.

questions.question:
A Configuration Manager is reviewing the life cycle of CIs to ensure data accuracy, consistency, and relevance. The manager reviews the legacy status values and their equivalent CSDM life cycle stage and life cycle stage status values.

Where are these reviewed?
questions.explanation: Legacy CI status values and their equivalent CSDM life cycle stages are reviewed in the Life Cycle Mappings table (cmdb_lifecycle_mapping). This table maintains the mappings between legacy status conventions and the current CSDM framework, ensuring accurate CI classification and consistency across the platform.

questions.question:
A CMDB Data Manager must access the ServiceNow platform to create, publish, and manage policies that automate and govern CI lifecycle operations, ensuring that the CMDB stays healthy and efficient.

Where can the Data Manager perform these actions?
questions.explanation:
The Management view in CMDB Workspace provides the Data Manager tool for centrally creating, editing, reviewing, publishing, and tracking Data Manager policies. These policies automate CI lifecycle events and help maintain CMDB health.

**Learn more:** [Management view in CMDB Workspace](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb-workspace-mangmnt-view.html) · [Create a CMDB Data Manager policy](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/data-manager-create-policy-wrkspc.html)

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator needs to remove all Linux Servers in the organization that have not been updated in six months.

Which recommended action should the Administrator take in Data Manager?
questions.explanation:
CMDB Data Manager is a policy-driven framework for bulk CI life-cycle operations, including archival. An Archive policy can target the Linux Server CIs that meet the six-month no-update condition and archive them, removing them from the active CMDB data set.

**Learn more:** [Working with CMDB Data Manager](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb-data-management.html?contentId=NQFNcUM6_rfLuj9vR5vCmQ) · [Create a CMDB Data Manager policy](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/data-manager-create-policy-wrkspc.html)

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator aims to utilize CSDM life cycle field mappings to better align with CSDM best practices.

What is the next step to take after selecting the Enable Life Cycle Sync button?

options.label: A
options.text: Resolve any incomplete field mappings identified in the Discrepancy Report

options.label: B
options.text: Fix the incorrect values in the Life Cycle Stage to match legacy values

options.label: C
options.text: Activate the CSDM Life Cycle field mappings

questions.explanation: After enabling the CSDM Life Cycle Sync feature, the next step is to resolve incomplete field mappings identified in the Discrepancy Report. This ensures all legacy CI status fields are properly mapped to the new standardized Life Cycle Stage and Life Cycle Stage Status fields before migration is finalized.

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator needs to set a CI Class as a Principal Class.

Which CI Class Manager tab would need to be accessed?
questions.explanation:
In CI Class Manager, the Principal Class designation is a core class property configured on the Class Info > Basic Info tab, alongside other fundamental attributes like display name, table name, and icon.

**Learn more:** [Update the Principal Class filter](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/update-principal-class-filter.html)

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator needs to prevent duplicate CI creation from import sets that load data into the CMDB from vendor shipment files containing CI information.

How can the Administrator do this?

options.label: A
options.text: Set the coalesce on two mappings within the transform map

options.label: B
options.text: Create comparison rules in the IRE

options.label: C
options.text: Set the system property to utilize the IRE within transform maps

options.label: D
options.text: Use the CMDBTransformUtil API in the transform script

questions.explanation: Standard transform maps do not automatically invoke the Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE) for arbitrary import formats such as vendor shipment files; the supported way to route that data through IRE-based identification and reconciliation (and thereby avoid duplicate CI creation) is to call the CMDBTransformUtil API from the transform script. There is no generic system property that turns on IRE processing for a transform map, which rules out that option.

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator is considering whether to start using the playbooks provided on the CMDB Data Foundation Dashboard.

What are the benefits to support the decision to leverage this feature? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Offers automated scripts to resolve poorly performing metrics

options.label: B
options.text: Offers insight into the downstream impacts of poorly performing metrics

options.label: C
options.text: Offers remediation options to address and improve poorly performing metrics

options.label: D
options.text: Offers remediation templates to improve poorly performing metrics

questions.explanation: Playbooks on the CMDB Data Foundations Dashboard explain the downstream impact of a poorly performing metric (why it matters and what it affects) and present concrete remediation options for improving it. They provide guidance rather than automated scripts or prebuilt remediation templates.

questions.question:
A Configuration Manager is implementing end to end service modeling and wants to get help on status and playbooks for improving the quality.

What does the Configuration Manager reference to obtain guidance?
questions.explanation: The CSDM Data Foundations Dashboard is the guidance surface for end-to-end service modeling, tracking relationships between business services, application services, and the infrastructure that supports them, and providing playbooks tied to each metric that describe why it matters and how to remediate gaps. The CMDB Data Foundations Dashboard instead focuses on configuration item health (completeness of serial numbers, owners, and CI attributes) rather than service-layer modeling, and CMDB Workspace is an operational console rather than a source of prescriptive improvement playbooks.

questions.question: Where in CMDB Workspace can a CMDB 360/Multisource CMDB Saved Query be viewed and created?

options.label: A
options.text: Saved queries window on the Insight tab

options.label: C
options.text: Coverage window on the CMDB 360 tab

options.label: D
options.text: Saved queries window on the CMDB 360 tab

questions.explanation:
CMDB 360 queries are managed from the Saved queries area on the CMDB 360 view in CMDB Workspace. That area lets users view existing saved queries and create new CMDB 360 queries.

**Learn more:** [CMDB 360 experience in a workspace](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb360-exp-cmdb-workspace.html) · [Create a CMDB 360 Get Records query](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/workspc-mltsrc-query-get-records.html)

questions.question:
The CMDB Administrator has configured two Dynamic Reconciliation Rules in the ServiceNow Production Instance. The **Server** class has a Dynamic Reconciliation Rule that uses the largest value for the RAM field. The **Windows Server** class has a Dynamic Reconciliation Rule that uses the most reported value for the RAM field.

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783715866877-kk6jj32x.png)

Given the data above in the Multisource CMDB, which RAM value would be added to the CMDB for a **Server** CI?
questions.explanation:
A dynamic reconciliation rule configured to use the largest value selects the highest RAM value reported by all discovery sources. Of the reported values, 8.192 MB is the largest. Dynamic reconciliation rules select values from CMDB 360/Multisource CMDB data, and a child-class rule applies only to CIs of that child class.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Reconciliation rules](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/r_ReconciliationRulesPrinciples.html)

questions.question: What is one purpose or requirement of CMDB Data Manager in ServiceNow?

options.label: A
options.text: Encrypts archived records for enhanced security

options.label: B
options.text: Automates the enforcement of relationship rules between CIs in the CMDB

options.label: C
options.text: Automates the archival and deletion of records based on retention policies

questions.explanation:
CMDB Data Manager uses policies to automate and govern configuration item life-cycle operations, including archival and deletion, helping maintain a healthy CMDB according to defined retention needs.

**Learn more:** [CMDB data management](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb-data-management-landing.html)

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator installed a Service Graph Connector and customized a script transform.

What occurs on later upgrades if the default definition of the script transform is updated?

options.label: A
options.text: A skipped change is created and no change is made the script transform definition.

options.label: B
options.text: The Service Graph Connector upgrade refuses to start.

options.label: C
options.text: The upgrade stops and reports an error.

questions.explanation:
ServiceNow records customizations to baseline objects as customer updates. During an upgrade, it skips an incoming change to a customized object to avoid overwriting the customization and creates a skipped-change record for review.

**Learn more:** [Resolve a skipped update and set a resolution status](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/upgrade-management/um-resolve-skipped-update.html)

questions.question: What keeps the data volume in the CMDB manageable?
questions.explanation: Archive policies control CMDB data growth by moving eligible older records out of the active dataset, keeping the operational record volume manageable.

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator group aims to establish a process for receiving task notifications when the Support Group or Managed By Group fields are not populated for operational Linux servers stored in the CMDB.

Which ServiceNow modules can be leveraged to configure recommended fields and generate task records in cases where these fields are missing for Linux servers in the CMDB?

options.label: B
options.text: Technical Service Offerings and Dynamic CI groups

options.label: C
options.text: Dynamic CI groups and CMDB groups

options.label: D
options.text: CI Class Manager and Health Preferences

questions.explanation: CI Class Manager is used to configure Recommended Fields for specific CI classes (such as marking Support Group and Managed By Group as recommended for Linux Servers). Health Preferences is then configured to automatically generate task records whenever CIs fail health checks due to missing recommended fields, creating a closed-loop data remediation workflow.

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator must create a new CI class for an Internet of Things (IoT) Sensor in ServiceNow.

Which practices are recommended for this activity? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Add a new class under an appropriate parent class

options.label: C
options.text: Install or update the CMDB CI Class Models store application, and verify the class does not already exist

options.label: D
options.text: Delete an unused class, and replace it with the new one

questions.explanation:
A new CMDB CI class should extend an appropriate existing parent class, preserving the hierarchy and inheriting applicable attributes. The CMDB CI Class Models Store app provides supported class models and associated metadata, so it should be installed or updated and reviewed before creating a custom class to avoid duplicating an available model.

**Learn more:** [Create a CI class](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/t_CreateCIType.html) · [CMDB CI Class Models](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/cmdb-ci-class-models/cmdb-ci-class-models.html)

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator is assessing the health of the CMDB and finds that a large percentage of Hardware CIs lack serial numbers. The Administrator is concerned that this could result in duplicate CIs and wants to address the problem promptly.

What structured ServiceNow-provided guidelines are available to troubleshoot and remediate this issue?
questions.explanation:
The CMDB Data Foundations Dashboard surfaces CI data-quality indicators, such as Hardware CIs missing serial numbers, and links each low indicator directly to a structured, prescriptive remediation playbook (with Analyze/Fix/Govern data plays) aimed at preventing duplicate CIs. The CMDB Health Dashboard reports metrics but does not provide these structured remediation playbooks, and the CSDM-labeled options relate to service-modeling maturity rather than hardware CI attribute quality.

**Learn more:** [List of all "Get Well Playbooks" (CSDM & CMDB)](https://www.servicenow.com/community/cmdb-articles/list-of-all-quot-get-well-playbooks-quot-csdm-amp-cmdb/ta-p/2301917)

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator needs to import external data into the CMDB. Because the CMDB Administrator wants to reduce the risk of creating duplicates and updating information from unauthorized sources, it must be ensured that the Identification and Reconciliation API is not bypassed.

What is the recommended method for importing data into the CMDB while using the Identification and Reconciliation API?

options.label: B
options.text: Table API (REST API or SOAP API)

questions.explanation:
IntegrationHub ETL incorporates the Identification and Reconciliation Engine into its import process automatically. IRE applies identification rules to avoid duplicate CIs and reconciliation rules so that only authorized sources can update CI attributes.

**Learn more:** [IntegrationHub ETL](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/integration-hub-etl/integrationhub-etl.html) · [Identification and Reconciliation API](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/api-reference/rest-apis/c_IdentifyReconcileAPI.html)

questions.question:
A development team is working on a project, and an application will be deployed across many servers. Several security requirements must be verified to meet legal compliance obligations because the application will hold customer personal data (PII and PCI).

Where in the CSDM should the development team look to store the information that will be used to satisfy the audits?

options.label: A
options.text: Technology Management Service Offerings (Technical Service Offerings) and Dynamic CI Groups

questions.explanation:
Information Objects logically describe data exchanged between an application and a database and can identify sensitive data, including personally identifiable information. Mapping them to Business Applications lets risk and compliance functions determine and apply the appropriate controls, supplying the application-and-data context needed for audits.

**Learn more:** [Information objects](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/governance-risk-compliance/grc-risk-management-workspace/information-objects.html?contentId=t9dXZvqxqFocrmAMzw5IVw) · [Design domain of the CSDM framework](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/common-service-data-model-csdm/design-domain.html)

questions.question: Where can an administrator carry out Natural Language Queries (NLQ)?
questions.explanation:
ServiceNow Intelligent Search for CMDB supports everyday natural language queries and is integrated into the CMDB Workspace, including its Home view. [ServiceNow: Intelligent Search for CMDB](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/intelligent-search-cmdb.html?contentId=Co0gv5d8ES8Tbh1I9g3ORQ)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow — Intelligent Search for CMDB](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/intelligent-search-cmdb.html?contentId=Co0gv5d8ES8Tbh1I9g3ORQ)

questions.question:
The ITSM Manager wants to use Technology Management Offerings (Technical Service Offerings) to populate the support group of associated CIs.

What CSDM stage would this be completed in?
questions.explanation: Associating Technology Management Offerings with support groups is a capability tracked within the Walk CSDM maturity stage. Walk is where service offerings are linked to their supporting infrastructure and operational teams, including the designation of support groups responsible for each offering.

questions.question:
A retail organization needs to ensure that incidents affecting customer-facing services are resolved quickly to reduce potential revenue loss.

Which CSDM attribute is used to prioritize these services?

options.label: A
options.text: Assignment Group on the CI record

options.label: B
options.text: Affected CIs in the Incident record

options.label: C
options.text: Business Criticality in the Service Offering

options.label: D
options.text: Service classification in the Technical Service

questions.explanation: Business Criticality is set on the Service Offering (and rolls up from the underlying Application/Technical Services) and is the CSDM attribute that reflects how important a given consumption of a service is to the business, letting incident and risk processes prioritize customer-facing offerings to limit revenue impact.

questions.question:
A Configuration Manager wants to explore ServiceNow CMDB 360 saved queries to see if the reports can assist with managing of CMDB data.

What insights are gained from CMDB 360 queries? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Gaps in attribute data from different data sources

options.label: B
options.text: Unique CIs created from different data sources

options.label: C
options.text: Different attribute values from different data sources

options.label: D
options.text: Orphan CIs created from different data sources

options.label: E
options.text: Duplicate configuration items from different data sources

questions.explanation: CMDB 360 provides saved query types built specifically for multisource data-quality analysis, including a Find Gap query that surfaces gaps in attribute data across different data sources and a Compare Attribute Values query that highlights different attribute values reported by different sources for the same configuration item. Duplicate and orphan CI detection are handled through separate CMDB de-duplication tasks and health rules rather than through CMDB 360 saved queries, so those options do not describe the insight this feature delivers. **Learn more:** [CMDB 360](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/sg-workspace-insights-cmdb360.html)

questions.question:
A Change Manager wants to realize value from CSDM.

How does the Change Management process benefit from CSDM? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Identify blackout windows for the change

options.label: B
options.text: Determine the root cause of the change issue

options.label: C
options.text: Understand the impact of the change on services

questions.explanation:
CSDM provides service and CI context that lets Change Management assess a change’s impact on services and service offerings. It also supports dynamic routing of change requests, using relevant CI and service data to direct approvals and assignments.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Change Management use case](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/itsm-change-use-case-example.html?contentId=vwaj4D82o1kOU6fuGfuxsg)

questions.question:
A Manager needs information on how to correctly establish relationships between Infrastructure CIs, Technology Management Offerings (Technical Service Offerings), and Application Services within the CMDB.

Which CSDM domain would provide this information?
questions.explanation: The Service Delivery (Manage Technical Services) domain of CSDM governs Technical Services and Technical Service Offerings, which sit between the Application/Infrastructure layer and the business, so it is the domain that documents how Infrastructure CIs, Technical Service Offerings, and Application Services relate to one another for operational support.

questions.question:
The CMDB Administrator group seeks to filler specific CI classes that display on the CMDB Health Dashboard. This ensures that only relevant data is displayed, excluding items that are not ready for management.

Which feature can the group utilize to achieve this goal?
questions.explanation: Health Inclusion Rules let administrators scope which CI classes (and which conditions) are evaluated on the CMDB Health Dashboard, so classes that are not yet ready for management can be excluded from the displayed health data. Identification and Reconciliation rules govern CI matching during import, not dashboard scoping, and there is no separate "Data Refresh Rules" feature.

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator needs to track which CIs and CI classes are missing key data.

Which CMDB Health Dashboard scorecard supports tracking this requirement?
questions.explanation: The Completeness scorecard on the CMDB Health Dashboard measures whether required and important attributes are populated, making it the correct tool for identifying CIs and CI classes that are missing key data. Correctness targets duplicates/orphans/staleness and Compliance targets audit rule violations, not missing field data.

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator wants to improve data quality associated with the CSDM.

Which action should the Administrator take to accomplish this goal?

options.label: A
options.text: Use the default configured CMDB Health Dashboard

options.label: C
options.text: Use the CSDM Data Foundation Dashboard

questions.explanation:
The CSDM Data Foundation Dashboard measures the health and quality of CSDM implementation data, including service-model relationships and missing required associations. Its indicators help identify and prioritize CSDM data-quality remediation.

**Learn more:** [CMDB and CSDM Data Foundations Dashboards release notes](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/store-release-notes/store-cmdb-rn-csdm-data-foundations-dashboards.html)

questions.question:
A CMDB CI Class Owner responsible for the Windows Servers needs to manage the Windows Server class.

Which CI Class Manager feature will help the CI Class Owner streamline this task?
questions.explanation: CI Class Manager's Pinned Classes feature lets a class owner keep frequently managed classes, such as Windows Server, readily accessible at the top of the class list instead of having to search for them each time, streamlining ongoing class management.

questions.question:
A CSDM Data Manager needs metrics on the alignment of product models, locations, and business units with best practices.

Which tab in the CSDM Data Foundations Dashboard provides this information?
questions.explanation: The Foundation tab of the CSDM Data Foundations Dashboard reports on the health and alignment of core reference data — including product models, locations, and business units (companies) — against CSDM best practices, since these OOB tables form the base layer that every other CSDM domain depends on.

questions.question:
The Configuration Manager is developing the justification to use the CMDB Data Foundations Dashboard.

Which benefits are aligned with using this dashboard? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: It enables monitoring and tracking of CMDB health over time.

options.label: B
options.text: It provides actionable insights to improve data quality and completeness.

options.label: C
options.text: It helps detect and eliminate duplicate records in the CMDB.

options.label: D
options.text: It automates the approval process for change management.

questions.explanation:
The CMDB Data Foundations dashboard monitors foundational CMDB health metrics and provides trend data for noncompliant configuration items over time. It evaluates CMDB configuration, customization, and data-management practices, highlighting risks and noncompliance and providing recommendations that support remediation and improvement of CMDB data quality and completeness.

**Learn more:** [CMDB Data Foundations dashboard](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb-data-foundations-dashboard.html?contentId=W3jznFFdpcXU5nbjXnCNqQ) · [CSDM and CMDB Data Foundations Dashboards](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/csdm-cmdb-foundations-dashboards.html?contentId=B97uS8oTWFVIS7z3SjSHWQ)

questions.question:
Configuration Management must ensure the quality of data for every CI in the CMDB.

Which CI data-quality areas are included in the CMDB Health Dashboard? (select 2)
questions.explanation:
The CMDB Health Correctness KPI includes the Orphan, Staleness and Duplicate metrics. Stale CIs are CIs not updated within the staleness rule's duration, and duplicate CIs are CIs matching an identification rule. Completeness measures CIs missing required or recommended fields, not missing CIs, and there are no downgraded or upgraded CI metrics.

**Learn more:** [CMDB Health KPIs and metrics](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/r_CMDBHealthMetrics.html) · [Overview of CMDB Health](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/overview-cmdb-health.html)

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator wants to leverage the CMDB Data Foundations Dashboard.

What are benefits of using this application? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Checks that important data is valid and properly configured

options.label: B
options.text: Has a framework to create custom metrics for the CMDB

options.label: C
options.text: Provides playbooks to assist in the remediation of potential risks

options.label: D
options.text: Uses automation to remediate potential risks

questions.explanation: The CMDB Data Foundations Dashboard validates that important CI data is configured correctly and provides playbooks to guide remediation efforts. It does not offer a custom metrics creation framework or perform automatic remediation; instead, it uses predefined metrics and offers structured guidance through playbooks that administrators execute manually.

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator is asked to create a query using the CMDB Query Builder that displays all operational CIs belonging to a specific application service.

Which steps provide the desired outcome?

options.label: A
options.text: 1. Add the Business Application, Application Service, and Configuration Item classes to the canvas.2. Define a filter for the application service name and the operational status of the configuration items.3. Configure the relationship between the classes.4. Run the query.

options.label: B
options.text: 1. Add the Application Service and Configuration Item classes to the canvas.2. Configure the relationship between the classes.3. Define a filter for the application service name and the operational status of the configuration items.4. Run the query.

options.label: C
options.text: 1. Add the Application Service and Configuration Item classes to the canvas.2. Configure the relationship between the classes.3. Add the Operational Status and Name fields as columns.4. Run the query.

questions.explanation: Building this query only requires the Application Service and Configuration Item classes plus a relationship between them; the filter is what actually narrows the result set to CIs of that application service with an operational status. Adding an unnecessary Business Application class or merely adding output columns (without a filter) would not, by itself, restrict the returned CIs to the desired set. **Learn more:** [Use CMDB Query Builder](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/bundle/zurich-servicenow-platform/page/product/configuration-management/task/use-cmdb-query-builder.html)

questions.question: Using existing baseline Data Manager policies, what condition must a CI meet before it can be archived or deleted?

options.label: A
options.text: Be fully operational and in use

options.label: C
options.text: Be retired and in end of life

questions.explanation: Baseline CMDB Data Manager lifecycle policies (Retire, Archive, Delete) are designed to act on CIs that have already been identified as obsolete, so a CI must be retired and past its end-of-life before it becomes eligible for archival or deletion; being operational, critical, or merely inactive does not satisfy this lifecycle gate.

questions.question:
An Asset Manager wants to make sure that Asset records and CI records remain automatically synchronized.

How can the Manager accomplish this? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Ensure one-to-one physical mapping between Asset and CI

options.label: B
options.text: Ensure that scheduled jobs are run during off-business hours to ensure sync happens

options.label: C
options.text: Ensure that the business rule to update Asset fields on change on the CI table is active

options.label: D
options.text: Ensure that the business rule to update CI fields on change on the asset table is active

questions.explanation:
Asset and CI records are synchronized bidirectionally by the **Update Asset fields on change** business rule on the Configuration Item (`cmdb_ci`) table and the **Update CI fields on change** business rule on the Asset (`alm_asset`) table. The records must be logically associated, but synchronization does not require a one-to-one physical mapping or off-hours scheduled jobs.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Asset and CI management](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/yokohama/it-asset-management/hardware-asset-management/c_ManagingAssets.html)

questions.question: Which CMDB Data Manager policy type generates tasks that enable the assigned person to update fields on the CI record?
questions.explanation:
A Certification policy generates certification tasks for validating record data. When the applicable option is selected, certification task reviewers can update CI field values as part of certifying the CI.

**Learn more:** [Create a CMDB Data Manager policy](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/data-manager-create-policy-wrkspc.html)

questions.question:
An organization is updating the CMDB to include new asset types like IoT devices. Relevant CI classes need to be added and outdated ones need to be removed from the Principal Class filter to ensure accurate display in ITSM processes.

Which roles are needed to add or remove classes? (select 2)
questions.explanation: Adding or removing CI classes from the Principal Class filter requires two roles: personalize_dictionary (to modify schema/dictionary elements) and sn_cmdb_admin (to manage CMDB configuration). These permissions ensure proper control over CI class visibility in ITSM processes. The sn_csdm_admin role is not a valid ServiceNow role and does not grant the necessary access.

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator needs insights into how their CMDB is configured according to ServiceNow recommended practice.

Which should be used?
questions.explanation: The CMDB Data Foundations Dashboard specifically benchmarks an instance's setup and customizations against ServiceNow's recommended configuration practices (for example, whether standard relationship types have been altered or custom tables introduced), which is what the question is asking about. The CMDB Health Dashboard instead measures ongoing data quality (completeness, correctness, compliance) rather than whether the CMDB itself is configured per recommended practice.

questions.question:
A Configuration Manager manages a CI class in the CMDB. The identification rule or rules require an update.

Where can the Configuration Manager view and configure the existing identification rule or rules for the class? (select 2)
questions.explanation: $ad

questions.question:
During a CMDB implementation, a team member is tasked with ensuring the accuracy and completeness of CI data. This person is also responsible for maintaining data quality and resolving discrepancies.

Which role is responsible for these tasks?
questions.explanation: The Configuration Manager role is responsible for ensuring CI data accuracy and completeness, maintaining overall CMDB data quality, and resolving data discrepancies. This operational role focuses on day-to-day CI integrity and governance, distinct from architectural design (CMDB Architect) or asset financial management (IT Asset Manager).

questions.question:
The CMDB Administrator wants to leverage the Staleness metric from the CMDB Health Dashboard - Correctness Scorecard.

Which field is used to calculate the duration of this metric?
questions.explanation: The Staleness metric uses the Updated (sys_updated_on) field to calculate how long a CI has remained unchanged. This field captures any update timestamp, including scans by ServiceNow Discovery or third-party tools, even when no attribute values change. This ensures accurate detection of stale configurations.

questions.question:
Configuration Management requires an accurate inventory of devices to be represented in the CMDB.

Which are common use cases for Agent Client Collector (ACC)? (select 2)

options.label: B
options.text: Devices that intermittently connect to the network

questions.explanation:
Agent Client Collector provides agent-based discovery and inventory collection for intermittently active hosts and for devices in isolated or secure environments, including air-gapped environments. The installed agent can collect and later transmit device data when network-based discovery is impractical or unavailable.

**Learn more:** [Agent Client Collector — ServiceNow](https://www.servicenow.com/products/agent-client-collector.html) · [Exploring Agent Client Collector — ServiceNow Documentation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-operations-management/agent-client-collector/exploring-agent-client-collector.html)

questions.question:
A Configuration Management Process Owner needs to configure Data Manager for policy tasks to be correctly assigned and aligned with the group attribute assigned to a class in CI Class Manager.

Which is the recommended field to be used for a policy task assignment?
questions.explanation: The Managed By Group field, defined per class in CI Class Manager, is the group reference that CMDB Data Manager consumes when it assigns policy tasks (attestation, retire, archive, certification, delete) for the CIs belonging to that class.

questions.question: Given a list of service types in the platform, drag the appropriate service to its definition.

options.label: A
options.text: Logical representation of a deploy system or application stack. -> Application Service

options.label: B
options.text: Published to Service Owners and underpins one or more business or application Services. -> Technology Management Service (Technical Service)

options.label: C
options.text: Published to Business Users and underpins one or more business capabilities. -> Business Service

questions.explanation:
In ServiceNow CSDM, an application service is the logical representation of a deployed system or application stack. A technology management service, formerly called a technical service, is published to service owners and typically underpins business or application services. A business service is published to business users and implements one or more business capabilities.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow CSDM glossary](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/common-service-data-model-csdm/csdm-term-definitions.html?contentId=AotqRiG10h51UtErd7qjOw) · [ServiceNow Service Delivery domain](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/common-service-data-model-csdm/manage-tech-servs-domain.html)

matchingPairs.label: A
matchingPairs.prompt: Logical representation of a deploy system or application stack.

matchingPairs.label: B
matchingPairs.prompt: Published to Service Owners and underpins one or more business or application Services.

matchingPairs.label: C
matchingPairs.prompt: Published to Business Users and underpins one or more business capabilities.

questions.question: Which ServiceNow solutions automatically create relationships between CI Applications that are part of an Application Service? (select 2)
questions.explanation: Discovery and Service Mapping both automatically trace and populate the dependency relationships between the Application CIs that make up an Application Service through horizontal/pattern-based discovery, whereas IntegrationHub ETL, Event Management, and Data Manager do not build these relationships on their own.

questions.question:
A ServiceNow Administrator wants to implement Service Graph Connectors to provide integrations to many third-party solutions that the company wants integrated into the CMDB.

Which categories of connectors are available to the Administrator? (select 2)
questions.explanation: ServiceNow groups Service Graph Connectors into categories such as Cloud (for example AWS, Azure) and Observability (for example Datadog, Dynatrace, AppDynamics); DevOps and Workflow Automation are not published Service Graph Connector categories.

questions.question:
With CMDB 360/Multisource CMDB, Dynamic Reconciliation Rules are also enabled. At management’s request, a CMDB Administrator must configure multiple Dynamic Reconciliation Rules.

Which ‘Dynamic Rule Types’ are available in the ‘Create Reconciliation Rule’ wizard? (select 2)
questions.explanation: ServiceNow CMDB supports multiple dynamic reconciliation rule types for selecting authoritative values from multisource data. The available types include 'Smallest Value' (numeric minimum) and 'Most Reported' (value appearing most frequently across sources), allowing behavior-based rather than priority-based selection.

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator is using the Duplicate CI Remediator to address a de-duplication task. On the first lab of the wizard, the Main CI is selected.

Which attributes are used to identify the Main CI? (select 2)
questions.explanation: The Duplicate CI Remediator identifies the Main CI using Oldest Created and Most Related Items, since the longest-standing, most-connected record is least likely to break historical references, relationships, and downstream processes when the duplicates are merged.

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator needs to run the Services Have Owners Identified playbook to remediate issues displayed in the CMDB Data Foundations Dashboard.

Which remediation plays would be used? (select 2)

A CMDB Architect intends to build a CMDB using CSDM guidance.

Which CMDB tables will the architect use to build the CSDM sell/consume domain?

options.label: A
options.text: Business Capability, Information Object, Business Application

options.label: C
options.text: Application Service, Technology Management Service (Technical Service), Technology Management Offering (Technical Service Offering)

questions.explanation: The Sell/Consume domain of CSDM is built from the Business Service and Business Service Offering tables, which represent what is published and offered to business consumers, along with associated service commitments. Business Capability/Information Object/Business Application belong to the Design domain, and Application Service/Technical Service/Technical Service Offering belong to the Build and Technical Service Delivery domains respectively.

questions.question:
The Configuration Management team finds value in the reports from CMDB 360/Multisource CMDB and wants to use it for all CI data.

Which must be true in order for CMDB 360/Multisource CMDB to be able to report on and analyze that data?

options.label: A
options.text: Reconciliation rules with priorities must be configured.

options.label: B
options.text: The CI data must be from an authorized Service Graph Connector.

options.label: C
options.text: The CI data must go through the IRE.

options.label: D
options.text: ServiceNow Discovery must be used to populate the CI data.

questions.explanation:
CMDB 360 (Multisource CMDB) reports on a CI attribute per data source, and those per-source values are only recorded when the data enters the CMDB through the Identification and Reconciliation Engine. The IRE is what tags each incoming payload with its source and stores the competing values that CMDB 360 then compares, so data written directly to CMDB tables bypasses it and never appears in the multisource view.

Reconciliation rules with priorities decide which source wins for an attribute, but they operate inside the IRE rather than being the precondition for reporting. Multisource data is not restricted to Service Graph Connectors, and Discovery is only one possible source.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: CMDB Identification and Reconciliation (IRE)](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/c_CMDBIdentifyandReconcile.html)

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator wants to use the CMDB and CSDM Data Foundations Dashboard.

questions.question:
A global enterprise integrates data from multiple discovery sources such as ServiceNow Discovery, SCCM, AWS, and manual uploads to populate its CMDB. However, each discovery source categorizes the same CIs differently, leading to duplicate records and inconsistencies across the system. As a result, the CMDB team is struggling with data accuracy and standardization.

What actions does the CMDB team take to resolve the issue? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Allow each discovery source to define its own CI class, even if it results in inconsistencies

options.label: B
options.text: Implement and use identification and reconciliation rules to avoid duplicates and standardize CI classification

options.label: C
options.text: Create a custom script to manually adjust incoming data before storing it in the CMDB

options.label: D
options.text: Use CI Class Manager to establish standardized CI classes and attributes across all discovery sources

questions.explanation: Identification and reconciliation rules ensure that CIs discovered by different sources (Discovery, SCCM, AWS, manual imports) are matched to the same underlying record instead of creating duplicates, while CI Class Manager lets an administrator define standardized CI classes and attributes that every source maps into. Letting each source define its own classes (A) perpetuates the inconsistency, and manually scripting adjustments per source (C) is not a scalable or standardized data-governance practice.

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator has imported data into the ServiceNow CMDB from a third-party source using a Service Graph Connector. The Administrator wants to review specific field to field mappings for the import.

Which feature will show that information?
questions.explanation: IntegrationHub ETL is the editor used to view and modify the field-to-field mappings that a Service Graph Connector applies when transforming third-party source data into CMDB classes and attributes, letting an administrator inspect exactly how each source field maps to its target CMDB attribute. Integration Hub is the broader integration platform and does not itself expose per-field mapping detail, and there is no standard "CMDB Integrations Dashboard" feature for this purpose.

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator needs to ingest relevant data from Microsoft SCCM into the CMDB.

Which ingestion method brings the fastest time to value?
questions.explanation: Service Graph Connectors are certified, out-of-the-box integrations (including the SCCM connector) that come pre-built with Identification and Reconciliation Engine mappings and CI classes, so they deliver a faster time to value than building a custom Import Set, an IntegrationHub ETL flow, or deploying the Agent Client Collector. **Learn more:** [Service Graph Connector for Microsoft SCCM](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-graph-connectors/cmdb-integration-sccm.html)

questions.question: When importing data into the CMDB with import sets and transform maps, which script type must be added to ensure that the data is processed by the IRE?
questions.explanation:
To apply CMDB Identification and Reconciliation Engine processing to CIs imported through Import Sets, the transform map’s `onBefore` script calls the `CMDBTransformUtil` API. This runs identification and reconciliation during transformation and helps prevent duplicate CIs.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Apply IRE to Import Sets](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/identification-import-sets.html?contentId=w9Fvs_0lUCenKl~8AS684g)

questions.question:
A hospital has received a new CT Scanner. The inventory management team has created a catalog item doctors can use to schedule patients for scans.

What CSDM domain should the inventory management team map the catalog item to?
questions.explanation: A catalog item that doctors use to request and schedule a scan is a consumable representation of a service offering, which belongs to the Service Consumption (Sell/Consume) domain of CSDM — the domain that captures how consumers request and use services, as distinct from the Design, Build, or Technical Service Delivery domains that describe how the service is built and operated.

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator uses the CMDB Data Foundations Dashboard to gain insights into the CMDB. The results display low scores for several metrics.

Which actions can the CMDB Administrator take to improve the CMDB Health? (select 2)

options.label: B
options.text: Focus on metric(s) with Critical and High priorities

options.label: C
options.text: Adjust the metrics using exclusion rules to improve the scores

options.label: D

questions.explanation: Prioritizing the metrics flagged Critical and High focuses remediation effort where data-quality risk is greatest, and following the Remediation Playbooks linked beside each metric provides the guided analysis, fix, and governance steps needed to raise the score. Excluding CIs from scoring or simply purging inactive records changes what is measured rather than genuinely improving CMDB data quality.

questions.question:
A customer wants server records that were recently imported to be automatically reclassified into more specific CMDB classes after ServiceNow Discovery discovers them.

During discovery, existing Server [cmdb_ci_server] records are reclassified into the Linux [cmdb_ci_linux_server] and Windows Server [cmdb_ci_win_server] classes. Which reclassification operation took place?
questions.explanation: A class upgrade moves a configuration item from a generic parent CMDB class to a more specific child class. Linux Server and Windows Server are more specialized classes than Server, so reclassifying existing Server records into either class is a class upgrade.

questions.question:

questions.question:

questions.question:
A CMDB Configuration Manager is reviewing the metrics on the CMDB Health Dashboard's Correctness Scorecard. For the Duplicate metric in the Server class, it shows Healthy CIs/Evaluated as 59,000/60,000.

What does this indicate about the scope of server records calculated under this metric?

options.label: B
options.text: 60,000 server records are in scope for this metric

options.label: C
options.text: 59,000 Linux and 60,000 Windows servers records are in scope for this metric

options.label: D
options.text: 59,000 server records are in scope for this metric

questions.explanation: On the CMDB Health Dashboard, the "Evaluated" figure represents the total population of records in scope for that metric, while "Healthy" reflects the subset that passed the check (here, non-duplicate). questions.question: Which default user groups are available when setting up a CMDB Data Manager policy and specifying the task assignment with the Assignment type set to 'User Group Field'? (select 2)
questions.explanation: When configuring CMDB Data Manager policy task assignment with 'User Group Field' assignment type, the default user groups available are Managed By Group and Support Group. questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator is tasked with managing the CMDB and needs to define a new CI class to track a new type of equipment that has not been seen before.

questions.question:

ServiceNow's own maturity dashboard lists "Business Service Offerings with Application Service Relationship" as a Run-stage metric, reflecting that a Service Portfolio Manager can only trace which Application Services a Business Service Offering depends on once this stage's relationships are populated. questions.question:

questions.question:

questions.explanation: A well-populated CMDB lets Event Management bind alerts directly to the affected CIs and, through mapped business services, surface the business impact of those alerts so priority can be based on service criticality rather than raw event volume.

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator notices that CIs do not have a support group.

How can the support group be automatically populated and maintained on the CI record?

options.label: A
options.text: Technology Management Service Offering (Technical Service Offering)

questions.explanation: A Dynamic CI Group evaluates a defined query against the CMDB and automatically adds or removes CIs as they match or stop matching its criteria, and it can be configured to propagate its support group to every member CI so the field stays populated and current without manual maintenance. A Technical Service Offering can seed the initial support group value through a data sync, but ongoing propagation to individual CI records is carried out via the dynamic group mechanism, and once inherited the group persists on the CI even if the CI later falls outside the group's criteria. CI Class Manager governs class and attribute structure rather than support group assignment, and there is no ServiceNow artifact named simply "Technology Management Service" that performs this function.

questions.question:
A Configuration Management Process Owner is developing solution options to present to the technical governance board for ingesting custom CIs into the CMDB. The solution must follow best practice, minimize the cost of future work (technical debt), and ensure compliance with future upgrades.

Which solutions achieve this? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Repurposing a base CI class and rename attributes, as required

options.label: B
options.text: Extending an existing CI class table to accommodate the custom CI class attributes

options.label: C
options.text: Installing or upgrading the ‘CMDB CI Class Models’ store application to find a suitable existing CI class accommodating any new attributes

options.label: D
options.text: Extending an existing Asset class table to accommodate the custom CI class attributes

questions.explanation:
The CMDB CI Class Models Store app supplies supported class models that extend the CMDB hierarchy, including class descriptions, identification rules, identifier entries, and dependent relationships. Selecting a suitable supplied CI class avoids unnecessary customization; when that class requires additional data, extending the appropriate CI class table with the required attributes preserves the CMDB hierarchy and supported CI behavior. Renaming or repurposing base-class attributes changes the intended model, and Asset-class extensions do not model a custom CI class.

**Learn more:** [CMDB CI Class Models app](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/cmdb-ci-class-models/cmdb-ci-class-models.html) · [Class extensions for integrations](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/cmdb-ci-class-models/cmdb-ci-class-models-extend.html)

A Configuration Manager responsible for a specific region wants to use the CMDB Health Dashboard to improve the data quality of the CMDB for that region. The Configuration Manager only sees the overall score and grouped by CI Class.

options.label: B
options.text: Customize the CMDB Health Dashboard scheduled jobs to group the results by region

options.label: C
options.text: Create CMDB groups with type, health, by region

By default, the CMDB Health Dashboard runs globally and groups by CI Class. CMDB groups restrict scope to specific CI subsets, enabling regional health tracking and targeted remediation efforts.

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator finds duplicate CIs. One was created through a manual import, while the other was created by automated discovery. The discovered CI contains the most current IP address, whereas the manually imported CI has an accurate relationship to a critical business application.

How should the Administrator use the Duplicate CI Remediator to resolve this issue?

options.label: A
options.text: Retain the manually imported CI, and delete the discovered CI

options.label: B
options.text: Merge the two CIs automatically, retaining all attributes from the discovered CI

options.label: C
options.text: Retain the discovered CI, but merge the relationship from the manually imported CI

options.label: D
options.text: Retain the discovered CI, and delete the manually imported CI

questions.explanation:
The discovered CI should be retained as the main CI so its current IP address is preserved. Duplicate CI remediation allows relationships from a duplicate CI to be merged into the main CI, preserving the manually imported CI’s accurate relationship to the critical business application.
