questions.question:
A Windows administration team wants a grouping of CIs using CMDB groups.

Which methods can be used? (select 2)
questions.explanation: CMDB groups in ServiceNow can be populated using two query-based methods: saved queries (pre-defined queries stored in the system) and encoded queries (dynamic queries embedded in the group configuration). Both methods allow flexible, maintainable CI grouping.

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator knows that the CMDB Data Foundation Dashboard is a resource to monitor and improve data quality.

options.label: B
options.text: Provides the ability to configure health-related metrics

options.label: C
options.text: Provides key health-related metrics to make decisions

questions.explanation: The CMDB Data Foundation Dashboard exists to surface key health-related metrics so stakeholders can make informed decisions about CMDB data quality; it is a reporting surface rather than a place to resolve certification tasks or configure the metrics it displays.

questions.question:
CMDB class owners receive tasks in the **My Work** tab of CMDB Workspace.

Which CMDB management tool generates these tasks?
questions.explanation:
CMDB Data Manager generates and assigns data-compliance tasks—including attestation, certification, and life-cycle tasks—through its policies. CMDB Workspace’s My Work view is specifically used to manage those assigned CMDB Data Manager tasks.

**Learn more:** [CMDB Data Manager experience in CMDB Workspace and Service Graph Workspace](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/data-mgr-exp-cmdb-workspace.html) · [Set up CMDB Workspace](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/setup-cmdb-workspace.html)

questions.question:
A CMDB Configuration Manager reviews the Correctness Scorecard metrics on the CMDB Health Dashboard for the Server class, which contains a total of 60,000 servers in the CMDB.

For the Duplicate metric, **Healthy CIs/Evaluated** is 59,000/60,000.

For the Orphan metric, **Healthy CIs/Evaluated** is 45,000/50,000.

Which configuration accounts for the difference in the Server CI scope evaluated by the two metrics (60,000 vs. 50,000)?

options.label: A
options.text: The Duplicate metric has a CMDB Group configured for the Server class.

options.label: B
options.text: The Duplicate metric has a Health Inclusion rule configured for the Server class.

options.label: C
options.text: The Orphan metric has a Health Inclusion rule configured for the Server class.

options.label: D
options.text: The Orphan metric has a CMDB Group configured for the Server class.

questions.explanation:
A health inclusion rule specifies the criteria CIs must satisfy to be included in evaluation for the health metrics to which the rule applies. An inclusion rule applied to the Orphan metric can therefore limit that metric to 50,000 Server CIs, while Duplicate continues to evaluate all 60,000. CMDB Groups are used for Health Group dashboard views and do not produce this metric-specific class evaluation scope difference.

**Learn more:** [Create health inclusion rule](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/create-health-inclusion-rule-d72863e26622.html) · [View CMDB Health Dashboard](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/c_MonitorCMDBHealth.html)

questions.question:
A Configuration Management Governance team is transitioning from using legacy CMDB status fields to CSDM life cycle status fields.

Which table can be modified?

ServiceNow provides default mappings and supports adjusting or adding mappings for an organization’s legacy or custom status values.

questions.question:
The CMDB Configuration Manager uses the CI Class Manager to manage CI-class group ownership and must use the ownership value defined in the CI Class Manager.

When configuring a CMDB Data Manager policy, which group reference field should be configured?
questions.explanation:
CMDB Data Manager policy approvals use the CI's Managed by Group attribute. CI Class Manager can populate that attribute across every CI in a class from the class-level ownership value, allowing the designated owning group to be used for approval routing.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Working with CMDB Data Manager](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/en-US/bundle/yokohama-servicenow-platform/page/product/configuration-management/concept/cmdb-data-management.html) · [ServiceNow: Set groups for CIs](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/common-service-data-model-csdm/csdm-data-synchronize-enable.html)

questions.question:
A healthcare provider is experiencing a critical incident affecting its patient management system. To mitigate disruption effectively, the provider must identify the impacted users.

Which CSDM-related data should it use?

options.label: C
options.text: Service Offerings by Department or Location

questions.explanation:
Service offerings can contain service-subscription data for departments and locations, which identifies the business consumers who may be affected by an outage. This makes Service Offerings by Department or Location the relevant data for determining the impacted user population. [ServiceNow CSDM implementation stage — Run](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/common-service-data-model-csdm/csdm-implement-run-stage.html)

**Learn more:** [CSDM implementation stage — Run](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/common-service-data-model-csdm/csdm-implement-run-stage.html)

questions.question:
A Business Relationship Manager in an organization wants to implement Service Portfolio Management (SPM) and to present offerings to business consumers.

Which CSDM Domain does this align with?
questions.explanation: Presenting a catalog of consumable offerings to business customers is the purpose of the Service Consumption (Sell/Consume) domain of CSDM, which is where Service Portfolio Management surfaces Service Offerings and Business Services to consumers.

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator changes the query for the SCCM Service Graph Connector.

What is the impact of this change?

options.label: A
options.text: Any Scheduled Jobs for the SCCM Service Graph Connector will need to be configured.

options.label: B
options.text: Any updates for the SCCM Service Graph Connector will be skipped during the upgrade.

options.label: C
options.text: The Data Source for the SCCM Service Graph Connector will be marked as Inactive.

questions.explanation: Editing the out-of-box query on a Service Graph Connector customizes that record, and ServiceNow's upgrade engine treats customized OOTB artifacts as protected: it skips reapplying the vendor's updates to that record during subsequent upgrades rather than overwriting the admin's change.

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator wants to understand the tools available to prevent, address, and remediate duplicate CIs.

Match each feature to its corresponding outcome. Some options might not apply.

options.label: A
options.text: Can be assigned to groups for resolving duplicate CIs -> De-Duplication Tasks

options.label: B
options.text: Offers insight into duplicate CIs within the CMDB -> CMDB Health Dashboard Correctness Scorecard

options.label: C
options.text: Offers a solution to resolve de-duplication tasks in bulk -> De-Duplication Templates

options.label: D
options.text: Provides a wizard to resolve de-duplication tasks individually -> Duplicate CI Remediator

questions.explanation:
IRE places detected duplicate-CI sets into de-duplication tasks, which can be reviewed and assigned for remediation. The CMDB Health Correctness KPI includes the Duplicate metric. De-duplication templates apply preconfigured remediation settings to multiple tasks in bulk, while the Duplicate CI Remediator wizard reconciles the duplicate CIs in one task. Certification tasks are for recurring data verification, not duplicate-CI remediation.

**Learn more:** [Detecting duplicate CIs](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/id-detect-dup-ci.html) · [CMDB Health KPIs and metrics](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/r_CMDBHealthMetrics.html)

questions.question:
The CMDB Configuration Management team needs to manage de-duplication tasks created from data ingested into the CMDB through the Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE).

In which area of CMDB Workspace can they find these de-duplication tasks?

options.label: A
options.text: Important actions tile under the Home tab

options.label: B
options.text: CMDB feature adoption tile under the Insight tab

options.label: C
options.text: Total status tile under the My Work tab

questions.explanation:
IRE-generated de-duplication tasks are surfaced through de-duplication-related cards in the **Important actions** tile on the CMDB Workspace Home tab. These cards provide access to the de-duplication dashboard and libraries used to remediate the tasks.

**Learn more:** [CMDB Workspace store app](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/washingtondc/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb-workspace.html?contentId=_ynkUX12fuegOtdTOeNOow)

questions.question:
A Configuration Manager is planning to implement the CMDB.

What is the prescribed CSDM rollout sequence?
questions.explanation:
ServiceNow prescribes a staged CSDM implementation in which each stage builds on the prior stage: Foundation, Crawl, Walk, Run, and Fly.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow CSDM implementation stages](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/common-service-data-model-csdm/csdm-implementation-stages.html)

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator wants to ensure all short-lived CIs that have not been discovered in the past week are removed.

After retiring the CI records, which recommended action does the CMDB Administrator take?
questions.explanation: After retiring short-lived CIs, the CMDB Administrator should create a Delete Policy (note: the choice contains a typo: 'police' instead of 'policy'). A Delete Policy is the proper Data Manager construct for automating CI deletion based on defined criteria. Scheduled jobs execute policies behind the scenes but are not what the administrator configures directly.

questions.question:
A company needs to understand the required CSDM maturity level. Different stakeholders have identified several use cases they expect to support over time.

Which use case requires information objects?

options.label: A
options.text: The Event Operations team wants to automate their events into incident for operational actions.

options.label: B
options.text: The Business Service Management team wants to understand the operational impact for their consumer parties.

options.label: C
options.text: The Customer Service team wants to onboard pro-active case management.

options.label: D
options.text: The SecOps team wants to understand the operational risk in the Business Application context.

options.label: E
options.text: The Asset Management wants to understand to asset life cycle compliancy in a Business Application context.

questions.explanation:
Information objects identify the logical data a business application uses, including sensitive information such as PII, PCI DSS, and HIPAA data. Mapping those objects to business applications enables risk and compliance functions to apply and assess appropriate controls, supporting operational-risk analysis in the business-application context.

**Learn more:** [Information objects](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/governance-risk-compliance/grc-risk-management-workspace/information-objects.html) · [Design domain of the CSDM framework](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/common-service-data-model-csdm/design-domain.html)

questions.question:
A Configuration Manager needs to restrict the number of classes available in a Configuration Item reference field on an incident form.

How does the Manager set Principal Classes?

options.label: A
options.text: By using the Principal Class check box on the CI Class Manager's 'Basic Info' tab for a Class

options.label: B
options.text: By using the Principal Class check box on the CI Class Manager's 'Attributes' tab for a Class

options.label: C
options.text: By using the Principal Class attribute on the CI

options.label: D
options.text: By using the Principal Class check box on the CMDB Workspace

questions.explanation: Principal Classes are configured in ServiceNow's CI Class Manager on the 'Basic Info' tab. Checking the Principal Class checkbox designates a class as principal, restricting CI reference fields in forms to show only principal class options, reducing selection complexity.

questions.question:
A CMDB Architect intends to populate the CMDB using the CSDM guidance.

Which key stakeholders from the organization should be involved in decisions regarding population of the CMDB using the CSDM Crawl Stage?

options.label: A
options.text: Business Service Manager, Technology Service Owner

questions.explanation: The Crawl stage of CSDM centers on the Design/Build domain, where Application Services and the applications running on them are modeled; the key stakeholders for populating this data are the Application Owner and the Application Service Owner, who can validate the relationships between applications, their services, and technical components.

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator has a number of similar de-duplication tasks that need to be remediated in bulk.

How does the Administrator achieve this?

options.label: A
options.text: Utilize the Duplicate CI Remediator Wizard

options.label: B
options.text: Configure and run a custom de-duplication background script

options.label: C
options.text: Create de-duplication tasks manually and remediate each

options.label: D
options.text: Create and run a de-duplication template

questions.explanation: When many duplicate CI issues share the same resolution pattern, an administrator creates a de-duplication template that encodes the consolidation logic once and then runs it across all matching duplicate tasks in bulk, rather than resolving each duplicate individually through the Duplicate CI Remediator wizard or a custom script.

questions.question:
The CMDB Configuration Management team has successfully developed a healthy and trusted CMDB. They have integrated discovered infrastructure data, accurately referenced non-discoverable data (such as change and support group information), and made the CMDB service-aware using Service Mapping.

How will these improvements enhance the change management process? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Provides insight into the potential impact of the change

options.label: B
options.text: Ensures that no changes result in service downtime, regardless of planning or execution

options.label: C
options.text: Automatically schedules and deploys changes without human review or approval

options.label: D
options.text: Enables auto population of the assignment group field to dynamically route changes

questions.explanation: A service-aware CMDB with accurate CI relationships lets change assessors trace potential downstream impact before a change is submitted, and reliably referenced support-group data lets the platform automatically populate the assignment group so the change is routed to the right team. No level of CMDB quality can guarantee zero downtime or remove the need for human review and approval, so those outcomes are not realistic benefits.

questions.question:
A data center has many servers. The CMDB Administrator wants to confirm that all servers exist.

Which Data Manager policy type does the Administrator implement?
questions.explanation: Attestation is the Data Manager policy type used to confirm CI existence and validity. Attestation policies pose yes/no confirmation questions to assigned users, such as 'Does this server exist?', making it ideal for validating that all servers in a data center actually remain active and operational.

questions.question:
A CMDB Configuration Manager sets up the following data filter for a certification policy using CMDB Data Manager.

• Table: Server [cmdb_ci_server]

• Filter: Operating System | contains | Server OR Operating System | contains | Linux

Which operating systems are affected by this policy? (select 2)
questions.explanation: The certification filter matches any server whose Operating System value contains the substring "Server" or the substring "Linux". "Linux CentOS" contains "Linux", and "Windows Server 2022 Datacenter" contains "Server", so both are captured by the OR condition, while "AIX" and "Windows 2019 Datacenter" contain neither substring.

questions.question:
A health organization must track certain data (for example, regulated patient information) and its relation to Business Applications.

Which action does CSDM recommend to meet this goal?

options.label: A
options.text: Create fields on the Business Application record to mark the Business Application as containing patient information, and then ask the Business Application owner to mark the application as having patient information or not.

options.label: B
options.text: Work with the Database administration team to classify the data on each database that holds patient information, and then use Relationships to map that back to the Business Application.

options.label: C
options.text: Create an information Object to represent the patient information, and then link it through a relationship to the Business Application after consulting with the Application owner.

questions.explanation: CSDM recommends representing regulated data such as patient information as a distinct Information Object and linking it via a relationship to the relevant Business Application, in consultation with the application owner, rather than adding custom fields to the Business Application record or trying to infer the relationship indirectly from database classifications.

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator needs to use dynamic reconciliation rules.

Which feature must be enabled?
questions.explanation:
Dynamic reconciliation rules rely on CMDB 360 (formerly Multisource CMDB) data to select attribute values across discovery sources. CMDB 360 must therefore be enabled before dynamic reconciliation rules can be used.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow — Reconciliation rules](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/r_ReconciliationRulesPrinciples.html) · [ServiceNow — CMDB 360](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/multisource-cmdb.html?contentId=kKiSmxGqbed33QEjCQGspw)

questions.question:
The following identification rule for a CI class has been defined:

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783715867974-t942sqng.png)

Two new CI records are imported into the hardware class of the CMDB:

- CI1: The name of this CI record matches the name of an existing CI record in the CMDB.
- CI2: The IP address of this CI record matches the IP address of an existing CI record in the CMDB.

Which statement is correct based on the identification rule and the imported CI records?

options.label: A
options.text: CI1 will be inserted as new record and CI2 will be updated with matching record.

options.label: B
options.text: CI1 will be updated with matching record and CI2 will be inserted as new record.

options.label: C
options.text: CI1 and CI2 both will be updated with matching records.

options.label: D
options.text: CI1 and CI2 both will be inserted as new records.

questions.explanation:
A Hardware CI can be identified by its `name` criterion, so the matching CI1 record updates the existing CI. An IP-address match alone does not satisfy any displayed Hardware identifier entry; the Network Adapter entry requires `mac_address` and `name`. CI2 therefore has no applicable identifier match and is inserted as a new CI.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Identification rules](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/yokohama/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/c_IdentificationRules.html?contentId=2oeCw94yZxSkU7mYfV~fVg) · [ServiceNow: Hardware cmdb_ci_hardware class](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/class-hardware.html)

questions.question:
A Configuration Manager needs to ingest third-party CIs into the CMDB.

Which method minimizes the risk of technical debt?
questions.explanation: Service Graph Connectors are pre-built and ServiceNow-certified, using standardized IRE mappings and CI classes that are maintained centrally, so they avoid the ongoing custom upkeep that vendor-specific integrations, raw Table API calls, or hand-built Import Sets and Transform Maps typically accumulate as technical debt.

questions.question:
A Data Center Manager is using the CMDB CI Class Manager to define the relationship between Application Servers and the Applications that they host. The company has multiple Application Servers, each hosting one or more Applications.

Which relationship describes the Application Server table (`[cmdb_ci_app_server]`) and the Application table (`[cmdb_ci_appl]`)?
questions.explanation:
Application Servers can host multiple Applications, and an Application can be deployed on multiple Application Servers. This is therefore a many-to-many CI relationship. ServiceNow CMDB models CI-to-CI relationships through the CI Relationship [`cmdb_rel_ci`] table; the standard `Runs on::Runs` relationship models an application running on hosting infrastructure.

**Learn more:** [CI relationships in the CMDB](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/c_CIRelationships.html) · [Relationship governance rules](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/zurich/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/relationship-governance.html)

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator needs to configure a new application identification rule that considers the potential for the same application installed more than once on the same server.

Which is the best choice of a criterion attribute?
questions.explanation: When the same application is installed multiple times on a single server, Configuration File Path uniquely identifies each instance. Two instances cannot occupy the exact same directory path; for example, one might use /etc/apache/instance1/httpd.conf while another uses /etc/apache/instance2/httpd.conf. This ensures reliable reconciliation and duplicate prevention.

questions.question:
A Configuration Manager needs to enable a CMDB Data Manager policy to remove records from a CI Class while retaining the ability to restore them within a specified period.

Which policy type should the Configuration Manager create?
questions.explanation: An Archive policy moves records out of the base table into an archive table while keeping them recoverable for a defined retention window, unlike a Delete policy (permanent removal) or a Retire policy (CI stays in the table, just marked inactive).

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator needs to create a CMDB query that finds all databases in Seattle that are connected to application services. The query must also include incidents associated with those databases.

Which actions should the company take to build this query? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Add to the canvas the Incident table from the Non-CMDB Tables list

options.label: B
options.text: Add a filter to the database node for location=Seattle

options.label: C
options.text: Set the relationship level to ‘Up to 2nd level relationships’

options.label: D
options.text: Add property columns to the application service node

questions.explanation:
CMDB Query Builder filters can be applied to a node’s attributes, so a `location=Seattle` filter on the database node restricts the results to databases in Seattle. Incidents are included by adding the Incident table from the Non-CMDB Tables list and connecting it through its CI reference. Second-level relationships are only needed when CIs may be indirectly connected through another CI; selecting result-property columns does not add records to the query.

**Learn more:** [Build CMDB query](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/use-cmdb-query-builder.html)

questions.question:
The CMDB Health Dashboard uses three Key Performance Indicators (KPIs): Correctness, Compliance, and Completeness. Each KPI contains several sub-metrics.

Drag each applicable sub-metric to its KPI. Some options do not apply.
questions.explanation:
Completeness evaluates whether mandatory CI attributes are populated, so it uses Required. Compliance uses the results of CMDB audits. Correctness detects data-integrity problems, including orphan CIs.

**Learn more:** [CMDB Compliance](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/c_Compliance.html) · [Enable and configure a CMDB Health Dashboard job](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/t_EnableCMDBHealthDashboardJob.html)

questions.question: Drag and drop the CMDB Health Dashboard metric to its description.

options.label: A
options.text: CMDB records that represent the same physical or logical asset multiple times -> Duplicate

options.label: B
options.text: Fields necessary to create or update a CI record in the CMDB -> Required

options.label: C
options.text: CMDB records that no longer maintain their logical or physical relationships with other CIs -> Orphan

options.label: D
options.text: CMDB records that are no longer actively updated, but remain stored in the database -> Stale

options.label: E
options.text: Fields that support the accuracy, completeness, and usability of CI records in the CMDB -> Recommended

options.label: F
options.text: Actual values of specified fields are compared to the expected values defined in a template -> Audit

questions.explanation:
Duplicate identifies multiple CI records for the same asset. Required and recommended fields measure CMDB completeness: required fields are mandatory, while recommended fields improve the usefulness and quality of the CI record. Orphan and stale identify CIs with missing relationships and CIs not updated in the applicable period, respectively. Audit evaluates compliance by comparing actual CI data with expected template values.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: CMDB Health KPIs and metrics](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/r_CMDBHealthMetrics.html)

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator is managing group data from both the CI Class Manager and a Technical Service Offering for a specific class.

Cl Class Manager:

- Managed by Group = Enterprise IT Services

Technical Service Offering:

- Managed by Group = Windows Support
- Change Group = Change Management Team

What would be the Managed By Group for CIs from this class based on the configured values?
questions.explanation: ServiceNow applies field precedence for CI ownership attributes: Technical Service Offering settings override CI Class Manager settings, which override individual CI record values. Since the TSO specifies 'Windows Support' as the Managed By Group, that value takes precedence.

questions.question:
An organization must maintain non-discoverable attributes, such as warranty expiration dates, for hardware CIs. Automated discovery tools do not update these attributes.

Which method ensures that these attributes are accurately maintained for every CI?

options.label: A
options.text: Create a new CI class specifically for non-discoverable attributes

options.label: B
options.text: Use the CMDB Reconciliation Engine to update the attributes

options.label: C
options.text: Use a scheduled data import to update the attributes from an external source

questions.explanation:
A scheduled data import can repeatedly retrieve warranty data from its authoritative external source and update the corresponding hardware CI attributes. Import Sets can be scheduled or run on demand to transform imported data onto the required CMDB table. The CMDB Reconciliation Engine controls which sources may update attributes, but does not independently populate attribute values.

**Learn more:** [Populating the CMDB](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/c_OptionsToPopulateCMDB.html) · [Configuring CMDB Identification and Reconciliation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/configuring-ire.html)

questions.question:
A CMDB Data Owner has requested belter insights on the different data sources that make up the CMDB data set. The Platform Owner knows that the new Service Graph Connector Central plugin is just what is needed.

After installing the plugin, what workspace will have the new Service Graph Connector Central tab available?
questions.explanation: After installing the Service Graph Connector Central plugin, the new Service Graph Connector Central tab becomes available in the CMDB Workspace. The Discovery Admin Workspace is reserved for discovery scheduling and configuration, while there is no built-in Service Graph Connector Workspace.

questions.question: Which ServiceNow solution automatically creates relationships?
questions.explanation:
ServiceNow Discovery automatically discovers many relationships between configuration items and loads them into the CMDB as part of the discovery process.

**Learn more:** [CI relationships in the CMDB](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/c_CIRelationships.html)

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator utilizing the CMDB Data Foundations Dashboard sees an issue and wants to run a playbook.

Which types of documentation can they expect to be provided in a playbook? (select 2)
questions.explanation: CMDB Data Foundations Dashboard playbooks provide two primary documentation types: Problem Overview (high-level context explaining the issue and business impact) and Problem Analysis (step-by-step guidance to investigate and identify root causes). These sections guide administrators through systematic data quality remediation.

questions.question: How is the CMDB aligned to business processes? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Enables the CFO/CIO to track software licenses

options.label: B
options.text: Enhances decision-making and operational efficiency across the organization

options.label: C
options.text: Extends service delivery management to all enterprise departments

options.label: D
options.text: Provides a centralized view of configuration items and their relationships

questions.explanation: A well-modeled CMDB aligns to business processes by giving every stakeholder a single, trusted, centralized view of configuration items and their relationships, and by using that context (ownership, dependency, and impact) to enhance decision-making and operational efficiency across the organization.

questions.question:
A CMDB Manager wants to start adding CSDM design and planning (design) domain components into the CMDB.

Who is involved in this exercise? (select 2)
questions.explanation: Adding CSDM design domain components involves Enterprise Architects who shape the architectural direction and Application Owners who define operational responsibility. These roles collaborate to establish and document design-phase components in the CMDB.

questions.question:
A CMDB team has noticed that some hardware CIs are missing the serial number information, making it difficult to maintain data accuracy. The team needs a structured approach to identify and address these gaps.

Which accomplishes this task?
questions.explanation: The CMDB Data Foundations Dashboard tracks best-practice metrics such as hardware CIs missing serial numbers, and clicking into that flagged metric launches a CMDB Data Foundation (Get Well) Playbook that gives the team a structured path to identify and close the data gap. CI Class Manager and Service Graph Connectors are unrelated configuration/import tools, not gap-remediation guidance.

questions.question:
According to the Common Service Data Model (CSDM), a server team requests that a catalog item be created for infrastructure-upgrade requests.

Which role participates in initiating the request and defining the requirements?
questions.explanation:
Technology Service Owners are responsible for technology services that support infrastructure and delivery. They provide the operational service requirements for infrastructure-related catalog offerings, including requests for server infrastructure upgrades. ServiceNow identifies technology service owners as typical users for the infrastructure and delivery portions of the CSDM Service Delivery domain.

**Learn more:** [Service Delivery domain in the CSDM model](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/en-US/bundle/zurich-servicenow-platform/page/product/csdm-implementation/concept/manage-tech-servs-domain.html)

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator has a report in ServiceNow that lists all CMDB Services that do not have an owner and wants to use a ServiceNow Playbook.

What Governance process play can prevent this from recurring?

options.label: A
options.text: Set a default value on the Service Owner field so that is never empty

options.label: B
options.text: Make the field Owned by mandatory

options.label: C
options.text: Make the field Managed by mandatory on all CIs

questions.explanation: Making the Owned by field mandatory on the business service record is a governance ("Govern Data") play that prevents new or existing services from ever being saved without an owner, directly stopping the recurrence of unowned services. A default value could mask the issue with a placeholder owner rather than genuinely assign accountability, and making Managed by mandatory on CIs addresses a different field on a different record type.

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator has been asked to clean up duplicate CMDB records.

What is the preferred way to manage this work?

options.label: A
options.text: My Tasks in the Application Navigator

options.label: C
options.text: The de-duplication dashboard on the CMDB workspace

questions.explanation: The CMDB Workspace de-duplication dashboard is the centralized interface for identifying, reviewing, and managing remediation of duplicate configuration items, making it the preferred method for CMDB duplicate cleanup.

questions.question:
The CMDB Configuration Management team has successfully created a healthy, trusted CMDB. They have integrated discovered infrastructure data, accurately referenced non-discoverable data (such as change and support group information), and used Service Mapping to make the CMDB service-aware.

Which Incident form field is automatically populated after selecting a CI that references an appropriate support group?
questions.explanation: A CI’s Support Group identifies the team that provides operational support for that CI. Incident routing uses this value to populate the incident’s Assignment Group, directing the incident to the responsible support team. Change and approval groups serve change-management routing, and Managed by Group denotes CMDB stewardship.

questions.question:
An Enterprise Architect of a financial services company is working across the enterprise and wants to track their capabilities.

Which CSDM 5 domain is used?
questions.explanation: In CSDM 5, the Design and Planning (Design) domain holds the Business Capability model along with Business Applications and Information Objects, which is the data used by Enterprise Architecture to define and track organizational capabilities across the enterprise. This is distinct from Build (technical implementation), Service Delivery (technical operations), and Service Consumption (offerings and subscriptions), none of which model capabilities.

questions.question:
A Change Manager wants to streamline ITSM processes by automatically filling fields on the Change form when a CI is selected. The Configuration Management team is working to make sure that the Change Group field is populated for every managed CI.

As a result, which base system field on the incident form is automatically populated after a CI is selected?
questions.explanation:
The **Assignment group** is the base task field populated by the CI/service-offering assignment business rule when it is empty. ServiceNow documents that the default CI source is the **Change group** for change requests; for incidents, the default source is the CI Support group. The target field in either case is Assignment group.

**Learn more:** [Create a change request in Service Operations Workspace](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/service-operations-workspace/create-change-sow.html?contentId=p4pnL8ns1qG95ZReHPtNUg) · [Create an incident in ITSM Agent Workspace](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/washingtondc/it-service-management/create-incident-from-workspace.html)

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator has created several Technology Management Service Offerings (Technical Service Offerings) based on Dynamic CI Groups to better maintain group alignment for member CIs.

Which groups are synchronized to CIs from an offering that has a relationship with a Dynamic CI Group? (select 2)
questions.explanation:
A technology management offering can synchronize its Support group and Managed by group assignment attributes to CIs associated through a Dynamic CI Group. Approval Group and Owned by Group are not part of this group-attribute synchronization.

**Learn more:** [Using dynamic CI groups](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/common-service-data-model-csdm/csdm-data-synchronize.html)

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator has been assigned to collect information for a leadership presentation. The Administrator must provide metrics for Duplicate CIs, Orphan CIs, and Stale CIs.

Which scorecard on the CMDB Health Dashboard supplies this information?
questions.explanation:
The Correctness scorecard aggregates the Duplicate, Orphan, and Staleness metrics. These metrics assess CI data integrity through identification rules, orphan rules, and staleness rules.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: CMDB Health KPIs and metrics](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/r_CMDBHealthMetrics.html) · [ServiceNow: Overview of CMDB Health](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/overview-cmdb-health.html?contentId=d4GfyG~8g1ZaxinB7TWwrA)

questions.question:
Using CI Class Manager, the Tomcat identification rule has the following criterion attributes configured:

• Class

• Install Directory

Which identifier entry configuration option must be checked to attempt a match using the Application identification rule if no match is found using the Tomcat identification rule?
questions.explanation: Each identifier entry can be configured to "Allow fallback to parent's rules," which tells the IRE that if no match is found using the current class's identification rule (Tomcat), it should attempt to match using the parent class's rule (Application) instead.

questions.question:
A CMDB Configuration Manager intends to implement CMDB Data Manager delete and archive policies for all server records in the New York datacenter.

In which lifecycle state would servers be affected by these new policies?
questions.explanation: Best-practice CMDB Data Manager configuration defines a Retire policy that sets the Lifecycle Stage to End of Life, followed by an Archive (and later Delete) policy that acts on CIs already in that End of Life / Retired lifecycle stage, since assets should never be archived or deleted while still active. Delete and archive policies are therefore scoped to servers in the End of Life - Retired lifecycle state, not to CIs that are still in use or newly inventoried.

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator is assessing whether to monitor the metrics available on the CMDB Foundation Dashboard.

Which benefits support the decision to continuously monitor the results on this dashboard? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Provides a list of all CIs that failed health audits

options.label: B
options.text: Provides metrics for CIs Processed by the IRE

options.label: C
options.text: Provides metrics on active CIs updated in the last 90 days

options.label: D
options.text: Reports on all orphan CIs in the CMDB

questions.explanation:
The CMDB Data Foundations dashboard includes metrics for configuration items processed through the Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE) and for active hardware or virtual-machine CIs updated within the last 90 days. These metrics support ongoing monitoring of CMDB data-management practices.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: CMDB Data Foundations dashboard](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb-data-foundations-dashboard.html?contentId=W3jznFFdpcXU5nbjXnCNqQ)

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator wants to educate the team on the various actions that can be performed within the CMDB Workspace.

What actions can be initiated from the CMDB Workspace? (select 2)

options.label: D
options.text: Create a CMDB Data Manager certification policy

questions.explanation: The CMDB Workspace provides two key capabilities for administrators: duplicate remediation and Data Manager policy creation. Duplicate remediation tasks surface directly in the CMDB Workspace Home tab where administrators can act on them, while the Management tab within CMDB Workspace is specifically designed for creating and managing Data Manager certification policies. Creating CMDB classes and executing Discovery are performed in different modules (System Definition and Discovery, respectively).

questions.question:
A Configuration Management team has decided to begin using the CMDB 360/Multisource CMDB functionality.

Which system property must be enabled?
questions.explanation:
The `glide.identification_engine.multisource_enabled` property is the master switch that enables CMDB 360/Multisource CMDB. The CMDB-class and non-CMDB-class properties only control data capture scope, while the query maximum-limit property controls result volume.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: CMDB 360](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/multisource-cmdb.html?contentId=kKiSmxGqbed33QEjCQGspw)

questions.question:
A company wants to track regulatory compliance. ServiceNow has an artifact type called an information object as part of the CSDM framework.

What is the purpose of an information object?

options.label: A
options.text: It describes data in general on a group of Configuration Items.

options.label: B
options.text: It describes data exchanged between an API interface and an Application.

options.label: C
options.text: It describes the logical data to the Business Applications.

questions.explanation: An Information Object is a CSDM artifact that describes the logical data (such as PII, PCI, PHI, or other regulated data types) associated with a Business Application, enabling data governance, privacy, and regulatory-compliance tracking rather than describing a group of CIs or an API payload.

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator must determine which attributes were created specifically for the Windows Server class.

Which tab in the Attributes section should be used?
questions.explanation: The Added tab lists attributes introduced directly on the selected CI class, rather than attributes inherited from parent classes or derived through the class hierarchy. For the Windows Server class, it therefore identifies attributes created specifically for that class.

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator wants to start utilizing the CMDB Health Dashboard and its Key Performance Indicators.

What does the Administrator do to start using the dashboard?

options.label: A
options.text: Download the dashboard from the ServiceNow store

options.label: B
options.text: Nothing, the dashboard is activated by default

questions.explanation:
CMDB Health Dashboard scheduled jobs are disabled out of the box, so an administrator must activate them (via Scheduled Jobs or Health Preference settings) before KPI data will be collected and the dashboard will populate. The dashboard itself does not need to be downloaded from the store and is not enabled by default.

**Learn more:** [Enable and configure a CMDB Health Dashboard job](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/bundle/servicenow-platform/page/product/configuration-management/task/t_EnableCMDBHealthDashboardJob.html)

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator wants to leverage the Staleness metric from the CMDB Health Dashboard - Correctness Scorecard.

What is the default duration of this metric?
questions.explanation: The default duration of the Staleness metric in the CMDB Health Dashboard Correctness Scorecard is 60 days. Any CI not updated within this 60-day window is flagged as stale, triggering data quality alerts and remediation workflows to ensure timely CI validation and refresh.

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator needs to ensure that only relevant CIs from managed classes are displayed on Incident, Problem, and Change records.

Which checkbox must be selected in CI Class Manager for the CMDB Administrator to achieve this result?
questions.explanation:
The **Principal Class** designation identifies the CMDB classes that are in scope for operational processes, including incident, problem, and change management, and restricts CI list views to CIs from those selected classes.

**Learn more:** [Update the list of classes in the Principal Class filter](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/update-principal-class-filter.html) · [CMDB glossary](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb-glossary.html)

questions.question:
An Enterprise Architect must help the CMDB owner understand CSDM’s benefits.

Drag each CSDM domain to its corresponding benefit.

options.label: A
options.text: Understand CIs related to business application and related capabilities to identify redundancies, monitor costs and make better investment decisions around roadmap -> Design and Planning

options.label: B
options.text: Understand technical services, technical service offerings, service support and all relationships to underlying technology CIs -> Service Delivery

options.label: C
options.text: Understand business services and ownership, cost, scope of what is offered to the business/consumer and request access to the business services -> Service Consumption

options.label: D
options.text: Use the base system tables when implementing the CSDM to derive the highest value from ServiceNow products and the Now Platform -> Foundation

questions.explanation:
The Design and Planning domain contains business applications and business capabilities, supporting portfolio rationalization, cost analysis, redundancy identification, and roadmap decisions. Service Delivery models the operational technical services, their offerings and support, and the underlying technology CIs. Service Consumption models the business services and offerings that consumers can request. Foundation supplies the base-system reference data needed to implement CSDM and gain value from ServiceNow products.

**Learn more:** [Foundation domain in the CSDM model](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/common-service-data-model-csdm/foundation-domain.html) · [Design & Planning domain in the CSDM model](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/common-service-data-model-csdm/design-domain.html)

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator needs the fastest time to value solution for effectively ingesting, managing, and maintaining CIs and relationships.

Which management tool will accomplish this to import Windows computer data from SCCM?

options.label: A
options.text: IntegrationHub ETL connection to SCCM using Robust Transform Engine (RTE)

options.label: B
options.text: Import set using JDBC data source connection to SCCM using transform maps

questions.explanation: The SCCM Service Graph Connector is purpose-built with IRE-based mappings to ingest Windows computer data straight from SCCM, giving the fastest time to value compared with a custom IntegrationHub ETL/RTE build, a JDBC-based import set with transform maps, or the unrelated SCCM Usage Metering Spoke. **Learn more:** [Service Graph Connector for Microsoft SCCM](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-graph-connectors/cmdb-integration-sccm.html)

questions.question:
A Windows server is reclassified from the Server table [cmdb_ci_server] to the Windows Server table [cmdb_ci_win_server] when processed through the Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE).

Which process occurred?
questions.explanation: Reclassifying a CI from the generic Server class [cmdb_ci_server] to the more specific Windows Server class [cmdb_ci_win_server], a subclass one level down the same hierarchy branch, is a class upgrade: the CI moves to a more specific class and gains additional attributes without losing data. A switch would instead move the CI between peer classes on different branches (for example, Windows Server to Linux Server), and a downgrade would move it to a more generic parent class.

questions.question:
ServiceNow provides a suite of CMDB management tools to effectively ingest, manage, and maintain CIs and relationships.

Drag each design architecture to its management tool. Some options might not apply.

options.label: A
options.text: Agent Client Collector -> Automated agent-based solution running patterns

options.label: B
options.text: Import Sets -> Organization-built solution using transform maps

options.label: C
options.text: Service Graph Connector -> Pre-built store integration solutions that require minimal customization

options.label: D
options.text: ServiceNow Discovery -> Automated agentless solution running Automated agentless solution running patterns

options.label: E
options.text: Third-party integrations from other vendors (Does not apply)

questions.explanation: Import Sets use transform maps to load and transform organization-built data imports. Agent Client Collector is agent-based, while ServiceNow Discovery is agentless and runs discovery patterns. Service Graph Connectors provide prebuilt integrations, including Store-delivered connectors, that minimize custom development.

questions.question:
A Platform Data Owner wants to improve data quality by using several reconciliation rules across the five discovery sources in use. The Data Owner knows that CMDB 360/Multisource CMDB is the best option for managing and monitoring discovery sources, but the company does not currently hold the ITOM Discovery license required for CMDB 360/Multisource CMDB.

What can the Data Owner do in this situation?

options.label: A
options.text: ITOM Discovery needs to be purchased to take advantage of the multisource IRE Rules.

options.label: B
options.text: CMBD 360/Multisource is a platform product that can be used immediately.

options.label: C
options.text: The IRE reconciliation rules can use discovery source regardless of CMDB 360 being enabled.

CMDB 360/Multisource CMDB must be enabled through the ITOM Discovery License plugin. Its multisource and dynamic reconciliation capabilities therefore cannot be used without purchasing the required ITOM Discovery entitlement. [ServiceNow: CMDB 360](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/multisource-cmdb.html)

questions.question:
An organization utilizes multiple data sources to update its CMDB, each assigned a different priority level. A high-priority data source is scheduled to update server records weekly. However, due to an integration issue, the high-priority data source stops updating the records.

Which configuration can be used to allow a lower-priority data source to update records after a specified period of inactivity from the higher-priority source?
questions.explanation: Data Refresh Rules (or Data Refresh Timelines) enable lower-priority data sources to update records after a specified period of inactivity from a higher-priority source. This configuration allows failover to secondary sources when primary sources fail or stop updating, maintaining CMDB data freshness.

How can the class be set as a Principal Class?

questions.question:
A new custom class is required to represent a new application managed in the CMDB.

Which roles are the minimum required to add this custom CI class?

Creating a CMDB CI class requires permission to manage CMDB class definitions and to edit the underlying dictionary metadata. ServiceNow requires `sn_cmdb_admin` (or `itil_admin`) together with `personalize_dictionary` for this work.

questions.question:
The Apache Web Server Identification Rule has the following Criterion attributes:

Class -

Configuration file -

Version -

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783715923890-aewvrh0t.png)

Yesterday, an Apache Web Server CI was discovered during Service Mapping. Today, the application owner upgraded Apache to a different version and reran discovery of the service. What will occur in the CMDB?

options.label: A
options.text: The existing Apache Web Server CI will be reconciled and its version will be updated.

options.label: C
options.text: The Apache Web Server CI will be reclassified as a Web Server CI.

options.label: D
options.text: A new Apache Web Server CI is created.

questions.explanation:
CMDB identification rules use their configured criterion-attribute values as the unique set for matching a CI. Because Version is part of that set, a discovered Apache instance with a changed version does not match the existing CI’s identifier values. The Identification and Reconciliation Engine therefore inserts a new Apache Web Server CI rather than reconciling and updating the old one.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Identification rules](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/c_IdentificationRules.html?contentId=U78sTHkcRxmg~sYYjwgqgg)

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator wants to configure IRE rules for the CMDB. The CMDB Administrator opens CI Class Manager and sees the Health Inclusions Rules tab available under a CI Class.

How are these rules utilized by the IRE?

options.label: A
options.text: To narrow the scope of CIs included in the identification process

options.label: B
options.text: To reduce the data ingested into the CMDB

options.label: C
options.text: To reconcile specific attributes based on data sources

questions.explanation: Inclusion rules defined for a CI class limit which CIs are evaluated by the Identification and Reconciliation Engine, so only CIs meeting the specified condition (for example, an operational status of Operational) are subject to identification and duplicate processing, narrowing the effective scope of that class. This is distinct from reducing overall ingestion volume (B) or reconciling attribute values from multiple sources (C), which are functions of coalesce/reconciliation rules rather than inclusion rules.

Some steps are required to transition from different CMDB status attributes to life-cycle objects.

questions.explanation: A lifecycle stage records the high-level phase of a CI’s lifecycle, and lifecycle stage status records the detailed state within that phase. Lifecycle mappings translate legacy status values by table into the appropriate CSDM lifecycle stage/status pair. Lifecycle objects apply lifecycle definitions to CI types, which controls the available detailed status values.
