questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator is leveraging CI data as part of an Integrated Risk Management implementation and the Entity Scoping process. The Administrator wants to leverage the CSDM Data Foundations Dashboard playbooks under the Run tab.

Which CSDM relationships are leveraged using the CSDM playbooks? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Business Applications that have their relationships to Information Objects

options.label: B
options.text: Business Applications that have relationships to Application Services

options.label: C
options.text: Logical CIs that have relationships with Information Objects

options.label: D
options.text: Locations that have established parent records

questions.explanation: The Run-tab playbooks used for Integrated Risk Management and Entity Scoping check that Business Applications are related to the Information Objects describing the data they process (needed to scope regulatory/privacy risk) and that those same Business Applications are related to the Application Services that technically deliver them (needed to scope technical/operational risk).

questions.question:
A ServiceNow Administrator needs to create multiple new classes in the CMDB but wants to follow ServiceNow's best practices for naming CMDB tables to prevent technical debt.

Which is the starting prefix for all custom CMDB tables?
questions.explanation: ServiceNow naming conventions dictate that custom tables use the 'u_' prefix to indicate custom scope. For CMDB CI class tables specifically, the standard prefix is 'u_cmdb_ci_', ensuring consistency with global CMDB naming standards while clearly identifying custom versus out-of-the-box classes.

questions.question:
A Configuration Manager wants to manage manually maintained data attributes of CIs.

Which group values are automatically synchronized on CIs using Technology Management Offerings (Technical Service Offerings) and dynamic CI groups? (select 2)
questions.explanation: The CSDM Data Synchronization engine automatically cascades specific support group fields from Technical Service Offerings to CIs in associated dynamic groups: Change Group (for change management ownership) and Support Group (for operational support). This reduces manual maintenance and ensures consistency.

questions.question: What is the relationship between an application and a server?
questions.explanation: An application runs on a server, while the server runs the application. The appropriate directional CMDB relationship is `Runs on::Runs`.

questions.question:
The following Reconciliation Rules are configured for ServiceNow, Altiris, and SCCM:

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783715865443-f86r32lb.png)

Which statements are true? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Data collected with a discovery source of SCCM can update any record in the Windows Server [cmdb_ci_win_server] table because it has the highest priority number.

options.label: B
options.text: Data collected with a discovery source of ServiceNow can insert new records into the Windows Server [cmdb_ci_win_server] table, but cannot update records created by Altiris or SCCM.

options.label: C
options.text: Data collected with a discovery source of Altiris can update records inserted by SCCM into the Windows Server [cmdb_ci_win_server] table.

options.label: D
options.text: Data collected with a discovery source of SCCM can be inserted as new records in the Windows Server [cmdb_ci_win_server] table.

questions.explanation:
A reconciliation rule’s priority controls which discovery source is authorized to update CI data; the lower priority value takes precedence. Altiris (200) therefore has higher update authority than SCCM (300), so it can update records SCCM created. Reconciliation applies to updates rather than new inserts; without a separate data-source rule that prevents insertion, SCCM can create new Windows Server CI records. ServiceNow documents that reconciliation rules control update authorization and priority, while data-source rules are the mechanism used to prevent sources from inserting new CIs.

**Learn more:** [Configuring CMDB Identification and Reconciliation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/configuring-ire.html) · [CMDB Identification and Reconciliation (IRE)](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/c_CMDBIdentifyandReconcile.html?contentId=5Pc1~JMnu8BR49CU5K1qNg)

questions.question:
A Platform Owner is working with stakeholders in the manufacturing industry to align their CIs to the CSDM 5 framework. They must map production line monitoring systems to the correct CSDM domain.

Which CSDM 5 domain should the Platform Owner use?
questions.explanation:
Production line monitoring systems are operational systems supporting the delivery and management of a production environment. The Service Delivery domain contains deployed service instances, infrastructure, technologies, operational models, and their related CIs; it is the CSDM domain used to manage and support those operational environments.

**Learn more:** [Service Delivery domain in the CSDM model](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/common-service-data-model-csdm/manage-tech-servs-domain.html?contentId=Zcdqcop~zN9iRX_fwxNsWg) · [Operational Technology and CSDM tables](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/operational-technology/operational-technology-manager/ot-use-case.html?contentId=5GJOSuNIm5hFFXVc3UJzdg)

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator has taken over management of a ServiceNow instance and has determined there are multiple deficiencies in the CMDB. During review of the CMDB Data Foundations Dashboard, the Administrator sees that ServiceNow offers Remediation Playbooks.

How can Playbooks assist the Administrator in resolving these issues?

options.label: A
options.text: Playbooks can be installed in the instance to automatically fix issues.

options.label: B
options.text: Playbooks can help analyze and fix issues.

options.label: C
options.text: Playbooks can automatically track common CMDB issues and output metrics.

questions.explanation: Remediation Playbooks surfaced from the CMDB Data Foundations Dashboard are guided workflows that help an administrator analyze the root cause of a flagged issue and walk through steps to fix it; they are advisory tools, not scripts that auto-install and self-remediate, nor are they metrics-tracking mechanisms.

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator is preparing technical documentation for stakeholders that includes a list of attributes, Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE) rules, and recommended relationships for several classes.

Which centralized location does the CMDB Administrator use to gather this information?
questions.explanation:
CI Class Manager centrally displays and manages CMDB class definitions and their settings, including class attributes, IRE identification and reconciliation rules, and suggested relationships.

**Learn more:** [CI Class Manager](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/ci-class-manager-landing-page.html) · [Create a CI class](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/t_CreateCIType.html)

questions.question:
A Service Owner needs to view related items, such as Active Incidents and Planned Changes, directly on the home node of the Unified Map.

Which work area would allow the Service Owner to meet this goal?
questions.explanation: The Contextual side panel is the Unified Map work area that displays modules such as Related items, Attributes, and Application services for the selected node, and shows details for the home node when nothing else is selected — letting the Service Owner see active incidents and planned changes without leaving the map.

questions.question: Which of the following are business values of a CMDB? (select 2)
questions.explanation:
A CMDB centralizes configuration-item and dependency data, improving incident and change management through better impact assessment and faster resolution. Visibility into service dependencies and configuration health also supports stronger operational resilience by helping teams prevent, assess, and recover from disruptions.

**Learn more:** [What is a configuration management database (CMDB)?](https://www.servicenow.com/in/products/it-operations-management/what-is-cmdb.html) · [Change Management use case](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/itsm-change-use-case-example.html)

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator is comparing the Unified Map to the Service Mapping map.

What are additional capabilities of the Unified Map? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Number of levels displayed on a map can be modified

options.label: B
options.text: Visibility to an application and the host it is installed on

options.label: C
options.text: Map nodes can be filtered based on user preferences

options.label: D
options.text: Map can be zoomed in and out

questions.explanation: The Unified Map offers two additional capabilities beyond the Service Mapping map: the ability to modify the number of levels displayed (depth control for complex dependencies) and the ability to filter map nodes based on user preferences. Zoom functionality and application-to-host visibility are common features available on both mapping tools.

questions.question: What types of policies can be created within CMDB Data Manager? (select 2)
questions.explanation: CMDB Data Manager supports two primary end-of-life policy types: Archive policies move records to archive tables for compliance retention, and Retire policies mark CIs as retired to preserve historical data without cluttering active operations. Reconciliation, De-duplication, and Decommission are not Data Manager policy types.

questions.question:
The Change Management team in an organization wants to implement a Change across multiple CIs at the same time.

Which field on the Change Request form needs to be populated with a dynamic CI group?
questions.explanation: Placing a dynamic CI group in the Configuration Item field of the Change Request form causes the group itself to be tracked as the change's primary CI while all of the group's member CIs are automatically populated into the Affected CIs related list, letting one change record cover many CIs at once. Business Service and Service Offering fields identify the service context of the change rather than the specific set of items being changed.

questions.question: Where does a user with the appropriate role(s) review and manage the generated tasks after configuring CMDB Data Manager policies?

options.label: A
options.text: CMDB Health Dashboard > Duplicate CIs tab

questions.explanation: After configuring CMDB Data Manager policies, users review and manage generated tasks in the CMDB Workspace, specifically in the 'My Work' tab. This dedicated workspace provides a centralized view of all assigned data compliance tasks, including attestation, certification, and CI lifecycle management activities.

questions.question: What is the value of using the CMDB in security operations? (select 2)

options.label: B
options.text: Identifies the IT infrastructure with a vulnerability

options.label: C
options.text: Enables audits and attestations across CIs

options.label: D
options.text: Allows security team to assess and remediate an incident

questions.explanation: The CMDB tells the security team exactly which infrastructure hosts a vulnerable component and provides the CI, relationship, and service context needed to assess an incident's impact and drive remediation; it does not resolve vulnerabilities on its own.

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator is tasked with moving various CMDB status attributes to life-cycle objects. The Administrator chooses to configure this by using the ‘reverse sync choice’ option.

Which reverse sync choice attribute should the Administrator select?

options.label: A
options.text: If the attribute is set to ‘false’, then the legacy state value changes the life cycle value.

options.label: B
options.text: If the attribute is set to ‘true’, then the life cycle value changes the legacy state value.

options.label: C
options.text: If the attribute is set to ‘true’, then the legacy state value changes the life cycle value.

options.label: D
options.text: If the attribute is set to ‘false’, then the life cycle value changes the legacy state value.

questions.explanation:
A life-cycle mapping normally uses a legacy status value as the source to set the CSDM life-cycle value pair. Enabling reverse synchronization reverses that direction, so the life-cycle value updates the legacy state value.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Life cycle mapping form](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/common-service-data-model-csdm/csdm-life-cycle-mapping-form.html?contentId=pqCEWiVx6dheaSNluvD9~g) · [ServiceNow: Specify how to map legacy life-cycle states to CMDB states](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/washingtondc/servicenow-platform/common-service-data-model-csdm/create-life-cycle-migration.html)

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator is assessing whether to monitor the metrics available on the CMDB Foundation Dashboard continuously.

Which benefits justify continually monitoring this dashboard’s results? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Provides a list of all CIs that failed health audits

options.label: B
options.text: Provides metrics for CIs Processed by the IRE

options.label: C
options.text: Provides metrics on active CIs updated in the last 90 days

options.label: D
options.text: Reports on all orphan CIs in the CMDB

questions.explanation:
The CMDB Data Foundations Dashboard reports the percentage of qualifying active hardware and virtual-machine CIs processed through the Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE), and it includes an **Active CIs Updated in Last 90 Days** metric to identify stale CI data. These metrics support ongoing monitoring of CMDB data-management practices.

**Learn more:** [CMDB Data Foundations dashboard](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb-data-foundations-dashboard.html)

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator wants to create a CMDB 360 query in CMDB Workspace to determine whether reports can help manage CMDB data.

Which items can CMDB 360 query? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Gaps in attribute data from different data sources

options.label: B
options.text: Different attribute values from different data sources

options.label: C
options.text: Duplicate CIs created from different data sources

options.label: D
options.text: Unique CIs created from different data sources

questions.explanation:
CMDB 360 supports Find Gap queries to analyze gaps in data reported by discovery sources and Compare Attribute Values queries to identify CI attributes whose values differ across discovery sources or from the CMDB.

**Learn more:** [CMDB 360 experience in a workspace](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb360-exp-cmdb-workspace.html) · [Create a Compare Attribute Values query](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/workspc-mltsrc-query-comp-attr-value.html)

questions.question:
Over time, a company’s CMDB has built up several custom CI classes for similar device types (for example: `u_cmdb_ci_custom_router`, `u_cmdb_ci_special_switch`, etc.). This has caused data fragmentation, reporting inefficiencies, and integration challenges.

How should the CMDB team resolve this issue? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Utilize CI Class Manager to consolidate custom classes into standard CMDB classes

options.label: B
options.text: Keep all existing custom classes to avoid potential risks associated with data migration

options.label: C
options.text: Delete all custom classes and manually recreate CIs under appropriate standard classes, ensuring proper classification

options.label: D
options.text: Move CIs from custom classes to standard ServiceNow classes, mapping attributes correctly

questions.explanation:
ServiceNow recommends rationalizing custom CMDB data by identifying the target CMDB classes, mapping attributes, and moving CIs from existing classes to the appropriate CMDB classes. CI Class Manager provides centralized management of the CMDB class hierarchy and class definitions, supporting class-model consolidation rather than preserving redundant custom classes. A controlled migration retains CIs and their related objects; deleting and manually recreating CIs risks losing data and relationships.

**Learn more:** [CI Class Manager](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/ci-class-manager-landing-page.html) · [Synchronize existing data](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/common-service-data-model-csdm/migrate.html)

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator is reviewing operational CI records that have no owners and are more than 1 year old.

Which recommended Data Manager action should the CMDB Administrator take to retire these records?
questions.explanation:
CMDB Data Manager uses life-cycle policies to govern bulk CI operations. A Retire policy can target CIs with no owner that are older than one year and retire them according to the active retirement definition for their CI class.

**Learn more:** [Working with CMDB Data Manager](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb-data-management.html) · [Create a CMDB Data Manager policy](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/data-manager-create-policy-wrkspc.html)

questions.question:
An ACMDB Administrator wants to fully use the CMDB 360/Multisource CMDB feature.

How does this feature help? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Automatically stores last record from each discovery source for view and assignment

options.label: B
options.text: Allows the CMDB to recompute after a reconciliation rule change, without waiting for a new data load

options.label: C
options.text: Allows defining reconciliation rules between discovery sources changing values

options.label: D
options.text: Provides a comprehensive up-to-date assessment of the company’s CMDB quality

questions.explanation:
CMDB 360 preserves raw data for each CI and discovery-source combination, including values not selected by reconciliation. Administrators can modify reconciliation rules and recompute CMDB data using those retained values without waiting for another data load. It also supports dynamic reconciliation rules that determine how values from multiple discovery sources are reconciled.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow CMDB 360 documentation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/multisource-cmdb.html?contentId=kKiSmxGqbed33QEjCQGspw)

questions.question:
A CMDB Manager is at the crawl stage of their CMDB journey and wants to follow the Common Service Data Model.

Which domains would be addressed? (select 2)
questions.explanation:
The crawl stage models business applications and application services together with their discoverable supporting CIs. Business applications are in the Design domain, and application services and their operational infrastructure are in the Manage Technical Services domain. Foundation establishes prerequisite referential data in a separate implementation stage.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow CSDM 2.0 White Paper — Crawl stage](https://www.servicenow.com/community/s/cgfwn76974/attachments/cgfwn76974/architect-forum/1786/1/CSDM%202.0%20White%20Paper%20final.pdf) · [ServiceNow CSDM implementation stages](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/common-service-data-model-csdm/csdm-implementation-stages.html)

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator is working in CMDB Workspace and has enabled Multisource CMDB.

Which tab is now populated when Multisource CMDB is enabled?
questions.explanation:
Multisource CMDB functionality is provided through the CMDB 360 experience in CMDB Workspace. The CMDB 360 view displays and analyzes data from the discovery sources that report CI attribute values.

**Learn more:** [CMDB 360](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/multisource-cmdb.html) · [CMDB 360 view in CMDB Workspace](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb-workspace-cmdb360-view.html)

questions.question:
As part of a CMDB improvement initiative, a team is assessing the effectiveness of the CMDB Data Foundations Dashboard.

Which describes a key benefit of the dashboard?

options.label: A
options.text: Automates the resolution of all CMDB data issues

options.label: B
options.text: Improves visibility into CMDB health and data quality

options.label: C
options.text: Eliminates the need for CMDB audits

questions.explanation:
The CMDB Data Foundations Dashboard provides metrics and insights that help teams monitor CMDB health, validate data and configurations, and identify risks affecting data quality. It supports visibility and remediation planning rather than automatically resolving all issues or replacing audits.

**Learn more:** [CMDB Data Foundations dashboard](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb-data-foundations-dashboard.html)

questions.question: Within the CMDB Workspace Intelligent Search UI element, which option is an alternative to using Natural Language Query (NLQ)?
questions.explanation:
CMDB Workspace Intelligent Search offers conditional search as an alternative to NLQ. Conditional search uses a basic condition builder to define searches for configuration items of a particular class.

**Learn more:** [Explore and Search view — ServiceNow documentation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/sg-workspace-search-explore-view.html?contentId=8zivXUAqLG7POsU03KWCPA)

questions.question: Which button is shown alongside the search results when a Natural Language Query (NLQ) that involves multiple tables is executed?
questions.explanation:
For an NLQ-generated CMDB query that contains more than one table, ServiceNow displays **View in Query Builder**. It opens the fully constructed query on the CMDB Query Builder canvas for further editing.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Intelligent Search for CMDB](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/intelligent-search-cmdb.html?contentId=Co0gv5d8ES8Tbh1I9g3ORQ)

questions.question: Where can a saved CMDB 360 query be created?
questions.explanation:
CMDB Query Builder is the dedicated ServiceNow tool for constructing multi-condition, multi-relationship queries that span multiple CMDB classes and related tables, and for saving, scheduling, and exporting those query definitions for reuse - capabilities a CMDB 360 style query depends on. CI Class Manager is used to manage the CI class hierarchy and schema rather than to build data queries, CMDB Reports is used for tabular and chart-based reporting rather than relationship-based CI queries, and CMDB Workspace is the broader workspace application that surfaces CI health and 360-degree views but relies on the Query Builder capability underneath it to actually construct and save a query.

**Learn more:** [CMDB Query Builder - ServiceNow Product Documentation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/csh?topicname=cmdb-query-builder-landing-page.html&version=latest)

questions.question:
A Configuration Manager manages the CMDB for a large enterprise and must establish rules for moving CIs through life-cycle stages including operational, retired, archived, and deleted.

Match each key life-cycle-management aspect to the activity needed to implement it.

options.label: A
options.text: CIs no longer required for active use but need to be retained for historical or compliance reasons -> Archive

options.label: B
options.text: Implement policies to periodically Verify CI data, ensuring it meets required standards -> Certify

options.label: C
options.text: Regular process to validate CI record is accurate -> Attest

options.label: D
options.text: Removes obsolete CIs in accordance with data retention polices and compliance requirements -> Delete

questions.explanation:
Archiving preserves inactive CIs without removing their historical record, while deletion removes obsolete records under retention rules. Certification policy validates CI attributes against required business values. Attestation is a scheduled review in which responsible users confirm or reject the CI information, maintaining CMDB accuracy.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Working with CMDB Data Manager](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb-data-management.html) · [ServiceNow: CIs attestation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/attesting-cis.html)

matchingPairs.label: A
matchingPairs.prompt: CIs no longer required for active use but need to be retained for historical or compliance reasons

matchingPairs.label: B
matchingPairs.prompt: Implement policies to periodically Verify CI data, ensuring it meets required standards

matchingPairs.label: C
matchingPairs.prompt: Regular process to validate CI record is accurate

matchingPairs.label: D
matchingPairs.prompt: Removes obsolete CIs in accordance with data retention polices and compliance requirements

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator notices that the **Hardware CIs Missing Serial Numbers** metric is trending upward in the CMDB Data Foundations Dashboard. Using the Get Well Playbook, the Administrator identifies the root cause and remediates the issue.

The Administrator now wants to run a monthly report to monitor the number of Hardware CIs without a serial number.

Which play would be used?
questions.explanation:
Data Governance covers the ongoing oversight and periodic review of CMDB data-quality results after remediation. A monthly report that tracks Hardware CIs lacking serial numbers is therefore a governance monitoring activity, whereas Analysis determines the cause and Fix performs the remediation. ServiceNow defines the Hardware CIs Missing Serial Numbers tile as the count of CIs that are non-compliant because their serial number is empty.

**Learn more:** [CMDB Data Foundations dashboard](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb-data-foundations-dashboard.html)

questions.question:
An Asset Manager and a Configuration Manager must synchronize fields between CIs and Assets.

How is this achieved in ServiceNow using the baseline system?
questions.explanation:
When an asset has a corresponding CI, ServiceNow keeps their records synchronized through two baseline Business Rules: one updates CI fields after asset changes, and the other updates asset fields after CI changes.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Asset and CI management](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-asset-management/hardware-asset-management/c_ManagingAssets.html)

questions.question:
The Configuration Management team finds the CMDB 360 dashboard useful and wants to continue using it.

What is displayed on the CMDB 360 Dashboard? (select 2)

options.label: C
options.text: CIs not reported by discovery sources

questions.explanation:
The CMDB 360 dashboard includes a Discovery sources tile showing the total number of discovery sources, and it includes a card for CIs not reported by discovery sources. Its purpose is to analyze multisource discovery data and discovery-source coverage, not to classify CIs by manual versus API entry.

**Learn more:** [CMDB 360 experience in a workspace](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb360-exp-cmdb-workspace.html) · [CMDB 360 view in CMDB Workspace](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb-workspace-cmdb360-view.html?contentId=6qlwFbsvvKrHpyRHz_9r6Q)

questions.question:
A customer uses Asset Management and Configuration Management processes and wants the asset and CI life cycles to remain synchronized. The CMDB Administrator has updated the **Hardware Status** field on a CI.

Which field is automatically synchronized on the related Asset record?
questions.explanation:
ServiceNow synchronizes a hardware CI’s Hardware Status with the associated asset’s State through the Asset-CI hardware status mapping, maintaining consistent lifecycle reporting. The mappings can also account for substates, but the CI Hardware Status change maps to the asset State field.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Asset and CI management](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-asset-management/hardware-asset-management/c_ManagingAssets.html) · [ServiceNow: Map asset state and CI hardware status](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-asset-management/asset-management/t_CreateAssetandCIHardwareStatusMapping.html?contentId=dyjOuoeFKd63m6LKxXfyCg)

questions.question: Which ServiceNow Store application is used to import data from various sources into the CMDB?
questions.explanation:
IntegrationHub ETL imports data from third-party sources, transforms and maps that data with ETL transform maps, and integrates it into CMDB classes.

**Learn more:** [IntegrationHub ETL](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/integration-hub-etl/integrationhub-etl.html) · [Populating the CMDB](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/c_OptionsToPopulateCMDB.html)

questions.question:
An IT operations team is making a change to an application environment and must ensure that the change is routed to the appropriate group for processing.

Which CSDM data should the team use?

options.label: A
options.text: The Service Subscription by User list for task assignments

options.label: B
options.text: The Assignment Group attribute on the CI

options.label: C
options.text: The Approval Group from the Business Service Offering

options.label: D
options.text: The Service Offering attribute to determine impacted environments

questions.explanation:
For change and change-task routing, the CI Assignment Group attribute identifies the group to which the work should be directed. The approval group controls approvals, while service offerings and service subscriptions do not provide the change-task routing value.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Change Management considerations](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/itsm-change-use-case-trouble.html)

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator needs to configure the CMDB Compliance scorecard and consequently creates several audits.

Which audit type is permitted in the CMDB Health Dashboard?
questions.explanation:
CMDB Health compliance scores are based on Desired State audits, which compare configuration items’ actual attributes and relationships with their defined desired state. ServiceNow documentation identifies Desired State audits as a source for CMDB Health audit scoring.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow CMDB Health domain separation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb-health-domain-separation.html) · [ServiceNow Desired State](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/c_DesiredState.html)

questions.question:
A Configuration Management Process Owner is preparing to deploy a ServiceNow CMDB and wants to minimize the risk of technical debt.

Which pillars of a successful data foundation will achieve this? (select 2)
questions.explanation:
ServiceNow’s successful CMDB data-foundation framework consists of Ingest, Govern, and Insight. Ingest establishes reliable population of CMDB data, while Govern maintains its quality, consistency, ownership, and lifecycle controls; these practices help prevent accumulated technical debt.

**Learn more:** [Platform: Configuration Management Database (CMDB) Knowledge and Resources](https://www.servicenow.com/community/cmdb-articles/platform-configuration-management-database-cmdb-knowledge-amp/ta-p/2381632) · [Autonomous IT Academy – CMDB Success Advisor + Dynamic IRE](https://www.servicenow.com/community/itsm-events/servicenow-exchange-autonomous-it-academy-cmdb-success-advisor/ev-p/3520795)

questions.question:
The CMDB Configuration Management team has successfully built a healthy, trusted CMDB. They have integrated discovered infrastructure data, accurately referenced non-discoverable data (such as change and support-group information), and used Service Mapping to make the CMDB service-aware.

How will these enhancements improve the incident management process? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Identify the impact of an incident on a service

options.label: B
options.text: Create knowledge base articles related to incident resolution

options.label: D
options.text: Automate the resolution of all incidents leveraging machine-learning

questions.explanation:
Service Mapping maintains the relationships between infrastructure configuration items and the digital services they support, allowing teams to identify the service impact of an incident. Reliable CMDB ownership and support-group data can also drive assignment rules that dynamically route an incident to the responsible team. Knowledge article creation and universal machine-learning resolution are not direct outcomes of CMDB health, discovery integration, and service mapping.

**Learn more:** [Drive service-aware operations with ServiceNow Service Mapping](https://www.servicenow.com/au/standard/resource-center/data-sheet/ds-service-mapping.html) · [ITSM – Now on Now – ServiceNow](https://www.servicenow.com/br/now-on-now/enhance-it-service-experience.html)

questions.question: Which CMDB Health Dashboard metric helps improve the use of CMDB Data Manager retirement policies?
questions.explanation:
The Staleness metric measures CIs that have not been updated within the effective duration set by their staleness rule. Those outdated CIs can be targeted by CMDB Data Manager retirement policies to maintain a current CMDB.

**Learn more:** [CMDB Health KPIs and metrics](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/r_CMDBHealthMetrics.html) · [Working with CMDB Data Manager](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb-data-management.html)

questions.question:
An Asset Manager at a software start-up follows the company’s Change Management process to relocate several software development resources from their existing location to a new location.

To which CSDM domain do the resources managed through Change Management belong?
questions.explanation:
Locations are common referential data in CSDM and are stored in the Foundation domain. A relocation processed through Change Management updates that foundational location context; Change Management does not change the CSDM domain classification of the location data.

**Learn more:** [Foundation domain in the CSDM model](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/common-service-data-model-csdm/foundation-domain.html)

questions.question:
A company has recently acquired another organization and wants to unify its deployed applications in ServiceNow.

Which CSDM record type will help accomplish this?
questions.explanation:
A Business Application represents the software and infrastructure environments configured to provide a business function, including development, test, and production. It is the CSDM record for managing and rationalizing an application across its deployments, and it can relate to the corresponding Application Services that realize it operationally.

**Learn more:** [CSDM glossary](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/common-service-data-model-csdm/csdm-term-definitions.html) · [Design & Planning domain in the CSDM model](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/common-service-data-model-csdm/design-domain.html)

questions.question: Which use cases make use of the CMDB Data Manager? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Verifying all servers in the Seattle data center exist

options.label: B
options.text: Generating a report on all duplicate Linux servers located in the London data center

options.label: C
options.text: Identifying the discovery source that provides the most accurate server memory (RAM) value

options.label: D
options.text: Retiring all computers that have not been updated in the last 6 months

questions.explanation:
CMDB Data Manager creates policies for CI life-cycle operations. Its Attestation policy can verify CIs at a specified location, and its Retire policy can retire computers meeting defined conditions such as not having been updated for six months. Duplicate CI analysis and discovery-source authority for individual attributes are handled through de-duplication and identification/reconciliation capabilities, respectively.

**Learn more:** [Working with CMDB Data Manager](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb-data-management.html?contentId=NQFNcUM6_rfLuj9vR5vCmQ) · [Configuring CMDB Identification and Reconciliation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/configuring-ire.html)

questions.question: Where does the CMDB Administrator configure tasks for CIs identified as orphans?
questions.explanation:
In CMDB Health preferences, the **Health Metrics** configuration for the Orphan metric includes the **Create Task** setting. Enabling it causes a task to be created when a CI fails the orphan health test.

**Learn more:** [Configure KPI and metrics preferences](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/t_ConfigureCMDBHealthMetrics.html)

questions.question:
A facilities department wants to use ServiceNow to store location data `[cmn_location]`, but is concerned that other data sources could create duplicate records.

Why should facilities use the Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE)? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Prevents inserts from unwanted data sources

options.label: B
options.text: Uses relationships to determine insert or update of CI records

options.label: C
options.text: Uses unique identification to determine insert or update of CI records

options.label: D
options.text: Prevents updates from unwanted data sources

questions.explanation:
IRE uses identification rules or unique identifiers to determine whether incoming data matches an existing record, so it can update that record rather than create a duplicate. Reconciliation restricts record and attribute updates to authorized data sources, protecting data integrity when multiple sources contribute data. ServiceNow documents that IRE supports certain non-CMDB tables and centrally applies identification and reconciliation across data sources.

**Learn more:** [Exploring CMDB Identification and Reconciliation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/exploring-ire-d72863e17266.html) · [Components and process of Identification and Reconciliation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/c_CompsandProcessIDandReconcil.html)

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator is updating a server and sets its life cycle stage to **End of Life**.

Which values can be selected for the life cycle stage status? (select 2)
questions.explanation:
For tangible or physical CIs, the End of Life stage includes the statuses **Disposed** and **Donated**. A broken server is associated with a defective condition, while Charity is not a defined life-cycle stage status.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Life-cycle of tangible/physical CIs](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/common-service-data-model-csdm/csdm-lifecycle-df-tangible-physical.html?contentId=3~PQ6N9eSfEh8o1EbGazVQ)

questions.question: Drag the ServiceNow product to the outcome by using the CMDB.

options.label: A
options.text: Tracks the lifecycle of a CI -> Asset Management

options.label: B
options.text: Automates incident creation based on threshold configuration -> Event Management

options.label: C
options.text: Uses the CMDB to identify and resolve issues faster -> Incident Management

options.label: D
options.text: Benefits the impact on downstream CIs when planning for an upgrade -> Change Management

questions.explanation: Asset Management tracks configuration-item and asset lifecycle information. Event Management can create incidents from configured event thresholds. Incident Management relies on CMDB data to identify affected configuration items and speed resolution. Change Management uses CI relationships for downstream impact analysis when planning upgrades.

matchingPairs.label: A
matchingPairs.prompt: Tracks the lifecycle of a CI

matchingPairs.label: B
matchingPairs.prompt: Automates incident creation based on threshold configuration

matchingPairs.label: C
matchingPairs.prompt: Uses the CMDB to identify and resolve issues faster

matchingPairs.label: D
matchingPairs.prompt: Benefits the impact on downstream CIs when planning for an upgrade

questions.question:
An organization must ensure that whenever a parent CI’s Life Cycle Stage changes, the Life Cycle Stage for its child CIs is automatically updated.

What action should the organization take to accomplish this?

options.label: A
options.text: Create a new CI class for Life Cycle Stage management

options.label: B
options.text: Use a Transform Map to update Life Cycle Stage statuses

options.label: C
options.text: Use Data Manager to set up Life Cycle Stage automation

questions.explanation:
ServiceNow dependent CI management uses CMDB Data Manager to process life-cycle updates for dependent CIs affected by changes to a parent CI. Data Manager policies and dependent-CI processing provide the relationship-based automation needed for cascading CI life-cycle operations.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Dependent CIs management](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/manage-dependent-ci.html) · [ServiceNow: Working with CMDB Data Manager](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb-data-management.html)

questions.question:
A ServiceNow Process Owner wants to use Business Application records in ServiceNow to guide business decisions.

How would the Process Owner use them?

options.label: B
options.text: Impacted applications for a Change Request

questions.explanation:
Application rationalization uses Business Application portfolio data and indicators to support strategic decisions such as whether to invest in, sustain, migrate, or retire an application.

**Learn more:** [Rationalization of business applications](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-portfolio-management/eaw-rationalize-business-applications.html)

questions.question:
A Configuration Manager must ensure that every device in the CMDB has a unique serial number to prevent the risk of duplicate CIs being created.

Which management tool identifies CIs that lack serial numbers?
questions.explanation:
The CMDB Data Foundations Dashboard monitors CMDB health metrics, including the Hardware CIs Missing Serial Numbers tile. This metric identifies applicable hardware CIs with an empty serial number so they can be investigated and remediated, helping preserve CI identification quality.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: CMDB Data Foundations dashboard](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb-data-foundations-dashboard.html)

questions.question:
A Service Owner has used the Unified Map filter panel to show particular CI types and layers.

How can the Service Owner save the filter selections?

options.label: A
options.text: Save the filter options as a preset

options.label: B
options.text: Reconfigure the filter options each time

options.label: C
options.text: Create a favorite using the banner

questions.explanation:
Unified Map filter settings can be saved as a user preset and later applied to a map. This preserves selections such as CI classes and layer criteria for reuse.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Manage a user preset](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/unified-map/unified-map-manage-preset-filter.html?contentId=T_6rG8sI8KLHmmp7dr6iIw)

questions.question: During an automated discovery scan, a web server instance and its underlying server are both discovered and ingested into the CMDB. When both are created in the CMDB, what default relationship is established between the web server CI and the server CI?
questions.explanation:
ServiceNow Discovery creates a **Runs on::Runs** relationship from an application CI to the computer or server on which it runs. A web server CI therefore **Runs on** the underlying server CI, while the server **Runs** the web server.

**Learn more:** [Exploring Discovery](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-operations-management/discovery/c_GetStartedWithDiscovery.html?contentId=mUfKF_P9h8XjpV_X_9XkaQ) · [Create a Discovery process classification](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-operations-management/discovery/t_CreateAProcessClassification.html)

questions.question:
A company must ensure that its IT assets meet security and regulatory requirements. It wants to track compliance details—such as GDPR or HIPAA—against its CMDB objects.

Which approach can be used?

options.label: A
options.text: Associate compliance identifiers with CSDM objects

options.label: B
options.text: Create custom compliance identifiers in the CMDB

options.label: C
options.text: Use the Service Catalog to request compliance tracking for CSDM objects

questions.explanation:
Compliance identifiers can be associated with CSDM objects to record which security or regulatory obligations, such as GDPR or HIPAA, apply to each modeled asset or service. CSDM provides the CMDB-based data model and relationships used to organize these objects; CMDB identification rules instead uniquely identify CIs, and the Service Catalog does not provide the compliance-association mechanism.

**Learn more:** [CSDM data domains](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/common-service-data-model-csdm/csdm-conceptual-model.html) · [Identification rules](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/c_IdentificationRules.html)

questions.question:
An ACMDB Administrator has been assigned to improve CMDB health and bring the organization’s CMDB into alignment with ServiceNow best practices.

How does the CMDB Data Foundation Dashboard Playbook assist in this situation?

options.label: B
options.text: Integrates third party discovery tools automatically

options.label: C
options.text: Uses a step-by-step approach to improving CMDB data quality

questions.explanation:
The CMDB Data Foundation Dashboard identifies CMDB data-quality and best-practice issues, and its playbook links provide remediation guidance. This supplies a step-by-step approach for correcting data-quality problems and tracking improvement.

**Learn more:** [CMDB and CSDM Data Foundations Dashboards Introduction](https://www.servicenow.com/community/cmdb-articles/cmdb-and-csdm-data-foundations-dashboards-introduction/ta-p/3290419)

questions.question:
The CMDB Configuration Manager needs to ensure that every Windows Server has more than 4 GB of RAM.

Which metric in the CMDB Health Dashboard is configured?
questions.explanation:
The Audit metric evaluates CMDB data for compliance with predefined audit certificates or templates. A rule requiring Windows Server CIs to have more than 4 GB of RAM is an attribute-value compliance check, so it is configured as an audit.

**Learn more:** [CMDB Health KPIs and metrics](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/r_CMDBHealthMetrics.html) · [Overview of CMDB Health](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/overview-cmdb-health.html)

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator must display only principal CIs as selectable on a change management form.

Which class is recommended to designate as a Principal Class in this scenario?
questions.explanation:
Principal classes should represent business-critical, independently managed infrastructure CIs that have meaningful service impact and are in scope for operational processes such as change management. A Windows Server fits that role; a disk and a network adapter are dependent component CIs rather than principal service-impacting CIs.

**Learn more:** [Update Principal Class filter](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/update-principal-class-filter.html) · [Key CMDB success advisor concepts](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb-sa-key-concepts.html)

questions.question:
An application group is rolling out a new business application whose application component cannot be properly modeled by any existing CMDB class type. Therefore, a custom CI class will be created by following best practices and assuming that all CIs are ingested through the Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE).

Which items must be present—either created or inherited—when creating a new custom CI class that is a child of Application `[cmdb_ci_appl]` in the CMDB? (select 2)
questions.explanation:
IRE requires identification rules to uniquely identify incoming CIs and prevent duplicates, and reconciliation rules to determine which data sources may update CI attributes. For a new CMDB table, ServiceNow allows these rules to be inherited from the parent class when they exist, or created at the child or parent level.

**Learn more:** [Components and process of Identification and Reconciliation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/c_CompsandProcessIDandReconcil.html) · [Identification rules](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/c_IdentificationRules.html)

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator uses import sets to populate non-discoverable CI data through the `CMDBTransformUtil()` script.

Which transform-map attributes must be populated? (select 2)
questions.explanation:
CMDBTransformUtil uses CMDB Identification and Reconciliation to identify and update CIs, so transform-map field maps must define the incoming import-set attribute and the CMDB attribute it maps to: the Source field and Target field. Coalescing is not required for CI identification, and a serial number is required only when an applicable identification rule uses it.

**Learn more:** [CMDBTransformUtil - Global](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/server-api-reference/c_CMDBTransformUtilAPI.html) · [Create a field map](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/integrate-applications/system-import-sets/t_CreatingAFieldMap.html)

questions.question: What functionality on a CI record in the CMDB makes it easy to relate CIs to one another?
questions.explanation:
The CMDB Relationship Editor is the CI-level interface for creating and managing relationships between configuration items. ServiceNow documentation explicitly refers to using the CMDB relationship editor to associate two configuration items.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Application Portfolio Management documentation](https://downloads.docs.servicenow.com/pdf/enus/servicenow-zurich-application-portfolio-management-enus.pdf)

questions.question: Which ServiceNow capability provides predefined integrations specifically built to simplify integration with external systems?
questions.explanation:
Service Graph Connectors are predefined integrations that ingest third-party and API data into the CMDB, providing a simplified, standardized way to integrate external systems. Service Mapping, IRE, and ACC serve discovery/mapping, CMDB data-governance, and endpoint-collection functions rather than providing those predefined integrations.

**Learn more:** [Getting started with Service Graph Connectors](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb-sgc-intro.html)

questions.question: Which metric or metrics are available on the CMDB Health Dashboard Correctness Scorecard?
questions.explanation:
The CMDB Health Correctness KPI is composed of the Duplicate, Orphan, and Staleness metrics. Required and Recommended are Completeness metrics, while Audit is a Compliance metric.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: CMDB Health KPIs and metrics](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/r_CMDBHealthMetrics.html)

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator must configure CMDB 360/Multisource CMDB.

Match each system property to its functionality. Some options might not apply.

options.label: B
options.text: glide.identification_engine.multisource_cmdb_ci_enabled -> Enables capturing CMDB 360 data for CIs from CMDB classes

options.label: D
options.text: glide.identification_engine.multisource.recompute.max.ci.limit -> Maximum number of CIs that can be included in a CMDB 360 recompute operation

options.label: E
options.text: Enables capturing CMDB 360 data for CIs from non-CMDB classes (Does not apply)

questions.explanation:
The multisource_enabled property activates CMDB 360. The multisource_cmdb_ci_enabled property controls data capture for CI classes derived from cmdb_ci. The logger property enables CMDB 360 logging, and recompute.max.ci.limit caps the number of CIs included in a recompute operation. Capturing data for non-CMDB classes is controlled by a separate non_cmdb_ci_enabled property, so that option is unused.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow — CMDB 360](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/multisource-cmdb.html?contentId=kKiSmxGqbed33QEjCQGspw) · [ServiceNow — Components related to CMDB 360](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/de-DE/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/components-multisource-cmdb.html)

questions.question: Which roles are assigned to a user to configure or work on tasks created by CMDB Data Manager? (select 2)
questions.explanation: In the legacy CMDB Data Manager role model, `cmdb_dm_admin` grants administrative configuration access, and `cmdb_dm_user` grants access to work on Data Manager-generated tasks. These roles form the corresponding administrator and task-user pair.

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator plans to implement CSDM, including the modeling of Business Capabilities.

Which options are appropriate? (select 2)
questions.explanation:
A CSDM business capability is a high-level organizational capability that supports the business model or mission and is typically expressed as a task that achieves a business outcome. ServiceNow specifically identifies managing financials and providing IT support services as examples of business capabilities.

**Learn more:** [Design & Planning domain in the CSDM model](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/common-service-data-model-csdm/design-domain.html) · [CSDM glossary](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/common-service-data-model-csdm/csdm-term-definitions.html)

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator wants to create a reconciliation rule through CI Class Manager, but is not offered the option to choose between Static and Dynamic.

How can these options be made available?

options.label: D
options.text: Navigate to the ‘Reconciliation Rules’ module, and enable the ‘Dynamic Rules’ option

questions.explanation:
Static and Dynamic reconciliation-rule tiles in CI Class Manager require CMDB 360 (multisource CMDB) to be enabled. Setting `glide.identification_engine.multisource_enabled` activates that capability, allowing the rule-type choices to appear.

**Learn more:** [Create a CI reconciliation rule](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/create-reconciliation-rule.html) · [CMDB 360](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/multisource-cmdb.html?contentId=kKiSmxGqbed33QEjCQGspw)

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator knows there are duplicate records in the CMDB and wants to understand the effect of running the **CMDB Health Dashboard Correctness Score Calculation** job. The following duplicate CIs exist in the CMDB:

- Server A: Created on January 20, 2025
- Server A: Created on January 21, 2025
- Server A: Created on January 22, 2025

Which records will have their **Duplicate Of** field populated?

options.label: A
options.text: Server A: Created on January 20, 2025 and Created on January 22, 2025

options.label: B
options.text: Server A: Created on January 21, 2025 and Created on January 22, 2025

options.label: C
options.text: Server A: Created on January 20, 2025 and Created on January 21, 2025

questions.explanation:
For a duplicate CI set, one CI is the main CI and its `duplicate_of` field remains empty; every other CI has `duplicate_of` set to reference that main CI. The earliest-created Server A record, from January 20, 2025, remains the main CI, so the January 21 and January 22 records are populated as duplicates.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: CMDB Health KPIs and metrics](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/r_CMDBHealthMetrics.html) · [ServiceNow: Duplicate CIs remediation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/de-duplication-tasks.html)

questions.question:
A Configuration Management Process Owner must access Data Manager to configure CI Lifecycle Policies.

Which CMDB Workspace tabs provide this access? (select 2)
questions.explanation:
The **Home** view provides a Data Manager quick link, and the **Management** view provides the Data Manager tool for creating, editing, reviewing, and publishing Data Manager policies, including CI life-cycle policies. My Work is intended for assigned tasks rather than policy configuration.

**Learn more:** [Get started with CMDB Data Manager](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/data-manager-get-started-wrkspc.html) · [Management view in CMDB Workspace](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb-workspace-mangmnt-view.html)

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator understands that groups defined on a Technical Service Offering are synchronized to the related CIs.

Which groups are synchronized? (select 2)
questions.explanation:
Technical Service Offerings synchronize the Support group, Change group, and Managed by group attributes to associated CIs. Therefore, the applicable listed groups are Support Group and Managed by Group.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Docs: Groups for technology management offerings](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/common-service-data-model-csdm/csdm-enable-tso.html)

questions.question:
A Configuration Manager is importing data into the CMDB while preserving CMDB integrity. The Manager plans to use the Robust Transformation Engine (RTE).

Why does the Configuration Manager use the RTE?

options.label: A
options.text: It searches the CMDB for already existing CIs and updates the CIs with the latest data sets.

options.label: B
options.text: It imports data from an external data source and pushes it to the staging table.

options.label: C
options.text: It takes in the definition for how data should be converted from an object to the IRE.

options.label: D
options.text: It inserts records into the CMDB in the correct classes and avoids duplicate data.

questions.explanation:
The Robust Transform Engine maps and transforms raw source data from staging tables according to an ETL definition and creates payloads for the Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE). IRE performs CI identification, reconciliation, class insertion, and duplicate prevention.

**Learn more:** [IntegrationHub ETL](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/integration-hub-etl/integrationhub-etl.html?contentId=YWEzW4gBxOg2CQ9qzG60mQ) · [RTETransformer - Scoped](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/server-api-reference/RTETransScopedAPI.html)

questions.question:
Life cycle sync is enabled on a ServiceNow instance. The ITAM Administrator changes a group of servers to the **retired** state.

What is the out-of-the-box life cycle stage value for the CIs associated with those assets?
questions.explanation:
With life cycle sync, asset state/substate values are mapped to the CSDM life cycle stage and life cycle stage status of the associated CI. The Retired asset state (with substates such as Disposed, Sold, Donated, Vendor credit or Lease return) corresponds to the End of Life stage, which is the CSDM stage for decommissioned or disposed hardware; its statuses include Disposed, Donated, Sold, Vendor Credit and Lease Return. End of Operation is only an intermediate stage between Operational and the next stage (statuses such as Pending Evaluation or Pending Return), and Disposed is a life cycle stage status, not a stage.

**Learn more:** [Definitions of life-cycle values for tangible/physical CIs](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/zS6yb8e~gR8BPjeviYdV9g/qsb_05MdO8FnwZTVEvPaRA) · [How life-cycle values for Asset, CI, and IBI are synced](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/zS6yb8e~gR8BPjeviYdV9g/Q5GUDt9S1NnLHBgQt7CwwA)

questions.question:
A Configuration Manager observes that the CMDB Health Dashboard Completeness Key Performance Indicator (KPI) is low.

What can the Configuration Manager do to obtain a KPI that represents only managed CIs?

options.label: A
options.text: Nothing, the health score is calculated for the whole CMDB

options.label: B
options.text: Configure health inclusion rules for the relevant CI classes

options.label: C
options.text: Create a business rule to filter the CMDB health results

questions.explanation:
CMDB Health inclusion rules filter the CIs included in health calculations and shown on the CMDB Health Dashboard. Configuring rules for the applicable CI classes limits Completeness evaluation to the managed CIs that meet those rules.

**Learn more:** [Create health inclusion rule](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/create-health-inclusion-rule.html?contentId=RC3UPFdFos3RLVwryRAF_Q)

questions.question: How is an Application Service created with relationships to its underlying infrastructure?
questions.explanation:
Service Mapping discovers application services and builds maps of the devices, applications, configuration items, and relationships that support them. It therefore creates the application-service relationship view of underlying infrastructure.

**Learn more:** [Service Mapping](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-operations-management/service-mapping/c_ServiceMappingOverview.html) · [Service instances (Application services)](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/application-services.html)

questions.question:
A CMDB Administrator has built a complex CMDB query in ServiceNow with CMDB Query Builder. The query retrieves detailed information about business services, servers, and application services related to the 'Network Service! Another team is working on a similar project in a different ServiceNow instance and wants to use the complex query.

Which approach should the other team use to transfer the complex query to the other instance?

options.label: A
options.text: Export the query using an Export XML, then use the Import XML option on the other instance

options.label: B
options.text: Export the query as a Report and provide the other team with the exported file, and then import it as a new report in their instance

options.label: C
options.text: Export the query using an Update Set, then import the update set in the other instance

options.label: D
options.text: Export the query from within Query Builder, then the other team can use the import query to import it directly

questions.explanation:
CMDB Query Builder can export a saved CMDB query definition as an XML file from within Query Builder. The destination instance imports that file by using the **Import query** action in CMDB Query Builder, which makes the query available among its saved queries. Update-set transfer is an alternative maintained for backward compatibility.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Export and import a CMDB query](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/export-import-query.html)

questions.question:
The IRE has detected duplicates for a single CI.

Which CI will the IRE update?

options.label: A
options.text: The oldest CI determined by the creation date.

options.label: B
options.text: The newest CI determined by the creation date.

options.label: C
options.text: The CI with the most recent updated date.

questions.explanation:
When IRE detects duplicate CIs and processes them with duplicate skipping enabled, it selects and updates the oldest duplicate CI. That CI becomes the main CI, while the other records are marked as duplicates; age is determined by creation date.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Detecting duplicate CIs](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/id-detect-dup-ci.html?contentId=hFfrI_zlUnGeFaHBYwICEg)

questions.question:
When viewing a CMDB record, a CMDB Administrator wants to determine whether it is a duplicate CI.

Which field on the CI record identifies this?

options.label: B
options.text: The ‘Discovery Status’ field has a value of ‘Duplicate’.

questions.explanation:
ServiceNow marks duplicate CIs by populating the `duplicate_of` attribute (displayed as **Duplicate Of**) with a reference to the main CI. A populated value therefore identifies the CI as a duplicate.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow — Duplicate CIs remediation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/de-duplication-tasks.html)
